# Strata Storage — full documentation (for LLMs)

Zero-dependency universal storage library and Capacitor plugin. One unified
async/sync API across web, Android, iOS, and optional Firebase. This file is the
entire documentation site concatenated for one-shot ingestion. Canonical site:
https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com  ·  Index: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/llms.txt  ·  Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/strata-storage


================================================================================
# Filesystem Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/capacitor/filesystem
================================================================================

# Filesystem Adapter

Native file-system storage for iOS and Android via Capacitor.

> **v2.6.0:** `FilesystemAdapter` now has a real native backend on iOS and
> Android. `isAvailable()` returns `true` on both platforms. Prior versions
> had no native implementation and the adapter was effectively unavailable on
> device.
>
> **Pending on-device verification:** The native code is complete and
> code-reviewed. Simulator and real-device sign-off is tracked in
> [`docs/guides/platforms/device-verification.md`](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md).

## Overview

Each key is stored as a single JSON file inside a dedicated subdirectory of the
app's sandboxed storage area:

- **iOS:** `<NSDocumentsDirectory>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`
- **Android:** `<Context.getFilesDir()>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`

The file content is the full `StorageValue` wrapper serialised to JSON, so TTL,
tags, and metadata are preserved across a write-read cycle. Writes go through an
atomic staging step — the value is written to a temp file in a reserved
`strata_storage/.strata-staging/` subdirectory, then renamed into place. This is
designed to avoid replacing a stored value with a partial write; the crash path
still needs the device verification linked above.

On the web (non-Capacitor) platform `isAvailable()` returns `false` and all
calls are routed to the in-memory fallback.

### Capabilities

| Feature | Support |
|---------|---------|
| Persistence | ✅ Yes (app-sandboxed filesystem) |
| Synchronous | ❌ No (async I/O) |
| Observable | ✅ Yes |
| Searchable | ✅ Limited (key-prefix scan) |
| Iterable (`keys()`) | ✅ Yes |
| Capacity | Limited by available app storage on the device |
| Performance | File I/O speed (variable; slower than SQLite for many small keys) |
| TTL Support | ✅ Yes (stored in value wrapper) |
| Batch Support | ✅ Yes |
| Transaction Support | ❌ No |
| `size(true)` | ✅ Yes (v2.6.0+) |

## Usage

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { FilesystemAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['filesystem'],
});
storage.registerAdapter(new FilesystemAdapter());
await storage.refreshAdapters();

// Write a value
await storage.set('report_q1', { lines: 42, status: 'final' }, {
  storage: 'filesystem',
});

// Read it back
const report = await storage.get<{ lines: number; status: string }>('report_q1', {
  storage: 'filesystem',
});
console.log(report?.lines);  // 42
```

## API Reference

All methods follow the standard `BaseAdapter` contract. Key behaviours specific
to this adapter are noted below.

### `isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>`

Returns `true` when running inside a Capacitor app on iOS or Android. Returns
`false` in a browser context.

```typescript
const fsAdapter = new FilesystemAdapter();
const available = await fsAdapter.isAvailable();
// true on device, false in browser
```

### `get<T>(key: string): Promise<StorageValue<T> | null>`

Reads `strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json` and deserialises the stored
`StorageValue<T>` wrapper. Returns `null` when the file does not exist. Returns
`null` (treating the entry as a miss) when the file content is not valid JSON —
corrupt legacy files do not throw.

### `set<T>(key: string, value: StorageValue<T>): Promise<void>`

Serialises `value` to JSON and writes it via an atomic rename:

1. Write to `strata_storage/.strata-staging/<sanitised-key>.tmp`
2. Rename into `strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`

This prevents partial files from appearing if the process is interrupted.

### `remove(key: string): Promise<void>`

Deletes `strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`. No-op if the file does not exist.

### `clear(): Promise<void>`

Deletes every `.json` file in `strata_storage/`. Files in the staging
subdirectory are also removed. Does not delete the directory itself.

### `keys(pattern?: string): Promise<string[]>`

Lists `strata_storage/`, reverses the file-name sanitisation for each `.json`
file, and returns the original key strings. Temp files in `.strata-staging/` are never
included in this list — a key whose name resembles a temp file (e.g.
`"backup.tmp"`) is safely stored and returned by `keys()`.

If `pattern` is provided the returned array is filtered by prefix or glob.

### `size(detailed?: boolean): Promise<StorageSize>`

Sums the byte sizes of all `.json` files in `strata_storage/`.

```typescript
// Basic size
const basic = await fsAdapter.size();
// { total: 4096, count: 12 }

// Detailed breakdown (v2.6.0+)
const detail = await fsAdapter.size(true);
// {
//   total: 4096,
//   count: 12,
//   detailed: { keys: 240, values: 3600, metadata: 256 }
// }
```

`detailed.keys` is the byte sum of all key strings, `detailed.values` is the
byte sum of serialised values, and `detailed.metadata` covers timestamps, tags,
and metadata fields.

## Configuration

`FilesystemAdapter` currently takes no constructor options. The storage
subdirectory name (`strata_storage`) and the staging directory
(`strata_storage/.strata-staging`) are fixed.

```typescript
// No options — just instantiate
const fsAdapter = new FilesystemAdapter();
```

## Platform Notes

### iOS

Files are placed in the app's `NSDocumentsDirectory`, which means they are
included in iCloud backups by default. If you are storing large or
reconstruction-only data (caches, derived data), mark the files to exclude them
from backup by setting the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` resource value on the
directory — this is not done automatically by the adapter.

### Android

Files are placed in `Context.getFilesDir()`, the app-internal private storage
area. No filesystem permissions are required (no `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` or
`WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`).

`androidx.security:security-crypto 1.1.0` (stable) is required for v2.6.0 —
this dependency is used by the Secure adapter, not the Filesystem adapter, but
both live in the same Gradle build. The Filesystem adapter itself stores values
as plain JSON without additional OS-level encryption. For sensitive data, use the
[Secure adapter](./secure.md) instead.

## Use Cases

### Persisting Large Documents

The Filesystem adapter is most practical for values that are too large for
Preferences (intended for small values) or that map naturally to a single file — think
cached API responses, user-generated drafts, or exported reports.

```typescript
async function cacheApiResponse(endpoint: string, data: unknown) {
  // Use a hash of the endpoint as the key to avoid filesystem-illegal chars
  const key = `cache_${btoa(endpoint).replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9]/g, '_')}`;

  await storage.set(key, data, {
    storage: 'filesystem',
    ttl: 3_600_000, // 1 hour
  });
}
```

### Offline Document Store

```typescript
class DocumentStore {
  async save(id: string, content: string) {
    await storage.set(`doc_${id}`, { content, savedAt: Date.now() }, {
      storage: 'filesystem',
    });
  }

  async list(): Promise<string[]> {
    const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'filesystem' });
    return keys.filter(k => k.startsWith('doc_')).map(k => k.slice(4));
  }
}
```

## Limitations

- **No sub-directory hierarchy** — all files sit in a flat `strata_storage/`
  directory. Slashes in key names are sanitised to underscores; there is no
  nested folder structure per key.
- **No transactions** — unlike SQLite, concurrent writes to the same key can
  race. Use the adapter only from a single execution context at a time or add
  your own lock.
- **Slower than SQLite for many small keys** — each key requires a separate file
  I/O round-trip. For high-frequency reads/writes of small values, prefer the
  [SQLite adapter](./sqlite.md).
- **Not available in browser** — `isAvailable()` returns `false` outside a
  Capacitor runtime.

## See Also

- [Storage Adapters Overview](../README.md)
- [SQLite Adapter](./sqlite.md) — better choice for many small key-value pairs
- [Platform Guide — iOS](../../../guides/platforms/ios.md)
- [Platform Guide — Android](../../../guides/platforms/android.md)
- [Device Verification Guide](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md)

# Preferences Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/capacitor/preferences
================================================================================

# Preferences Adapter

Store small app settings in native iOS and Android preferences through Capacitor.

## Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'myapp' });
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' });
const theme = await storage.get<string>('theme', { storage: 'preferences' });
```

Call `registerCapacitorAdapters` in a native Capacitor app before the first native storage operation. The registration helper returns without registering native adapters in a browser.

## Configuration

`StrataConfig.adapters.preferences` accepts a boolean. It does not expose an App Group, key prefix, or iCloud sync option. Use the instance `namespace` to separate logical key groups.

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  namespace: 'settings',
  defaultStorages: ['preferences', 'memory'],
  adapters: { preferences: true },
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
```

For larger records, use the [SQLite adapter](./sqlite.md) or [Filesystem adapter](./filesystem.md). Use the [Secure adapter](./secure.md) for sensitive values.

## Verification

Native read, write, persistence, and availability still require iOS and Android device checks. See the [device verification guide](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md).


================================================================================
# Secure Storage Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/capacitor/secure
================================================================================

# Secure Storage Adapter

Store sensitive values through Strata Storage's native secure adapter in a Capacitor app.

## Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage();
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('session_token', token, {
  storage: 'secure',
  ttl: 3_600_000,
});
const savedToken = await storage.get<string>('session_token', { storage: 'secure' });
await storage.remove('session_token', { storage: 'secure' });
```

Call `registerCapacitorAdapters` before the first native operation. It registers no native adapter when running in a browser.

## Configuration and limits

`StrataConfig.adapters.secure` accepts a boolean. Per-operation `StorageOptions` supports `storage`, `ttl`, `encrypt`, and other common Strata options. It does **not** expose Keychain accessibility, a biometric requirement, or an authentication prompt. Do not rely on this adapter for a biometric confirmation flow.

Treat the stored values as credentials: keep keys scoped to the application, use a short TTL where appropriate, and remove them at sign-out. Native behavior and persistence need iOS and Android device verification; see the [device verification guide](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md).

## See also

- [Capacitor platform guide](../../../guides/platforms/capacitor.md)
- [Encryption guide](../../../guides/features/encryption.md)


================================================================================
# SQLite adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/capacitor/sqlite
================================================================================

# SQLite adapter

The optional Capacitor SQLite adapter stores Strata key/value records in a native SQLite database on iOS and Android. Strata's public API remains key/value based: it does not expose raw SQL, indexes or atomic SQL transactions through `storage`.

## Register and verify

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { SqliteAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['sqlite'] });
storage.registerAdapter(new SqliteAdapter());
await storage.refreshAdapters();

await storage.set('user:1', { age: 32, city: 'Lahore' }, {
  storage: 'sqlite',
});
const user = await storage.get<{ age: number; city: string }>('user:1', {
  storage: 'sqlite',
});
```

This needs a running Capacitor iOS or Android app and a synced native project. It cannot prove a native read from a browser tab. Repeat the read after app restart and follow the [device verification guide](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md).

## Separate native stores

`SqliteAdapter` accepts `database` and `table` constructor options. Use distinct instances when different domains need different physical stores:

```typescript
const settings = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['sqlite'] });
settings.registerAdapter(new SqliteAdapter({
  database: 'settings',
  table: 'preferences',
}));
await settings.refreshAdapters();

await settings.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'sqlite' });
```

Database and table identifiers are validated. Do not pass arbitrary user input as either name. The native implementation's multi-store and value-wrapper changes still require the project device matrix before a production claim.

## Query decoded values

`storage.query()` checks fields of the value returned by `get()`. It does not query the physical key, Strata wrapper metadata, or a `value.*` path:

```typescript
const adultsInLahore = await storage.query<{ age: number; city: string }>({
  age: { $gte: 18 },
  city: 'Lahore',
}, { storage: 'sqlite' });
```

To find keys by name, use `storage.keys(/^user:/, { storage: 'sqlite' })`. For a pending record, store `syncStatus` inside the value and query `{ syncStatus: 'pending' }`. Querying through Strata reads and evaluates decoded records; it is not a native indexed SQL query. If your app needs indexed SQL queries, use a native database API directly.

## Size and expiry

`SqliteAdapter.size(true)` returns a byte breakdown for keys, values and metadata in the native implementation. Numbers depend on the actual records and platform. Strata's TTL makes expired values read as missing, and `cleanupExpired()` can reclaim them. Verify these behaviours on the target device before relying on them.

## Transaction boundary

The adapter exposes a best-effort sequential batch internally; `capabilities.transactional` is false. A failed later operation does not roll back an earlier committed write. Build an application-level recovery path when several writes must succeed together.

The native backend, isolation, expiry and size paths are tracked in [device verification](../../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md). No simulator or physical-device result is claimed by this page.


================================================================================
# Storage adapters
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters
================================================================================

# Storage adapters

Strata Storage presents the same key/value operations to different storage backends. The selected adapter determines where values live and which platform can read them.

## Adapter map

| Adapter | Where it runs | What it stores | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Memory](./web/memory.md) | JavaScript runtime | Temporary values, cleared on reload | Included in the default web set |
| [LocalStorage](./web/localstorage.md) | Browser page | Persistent values for one origin | Included in the default web set |
| [SessionStorage](./web/sessionstorage.md) | Browser page | Values for one tab session | Included in the default web set |
| [IndexedDB](./web/indexeddb.md) | Browser page | Persistent key/value data | Included in the default web set |
| [Cookies](./web/cookies.md) | Browser page | Small values in browser cookies | Included in the default web set |
| [Cache](./web/cache.md) | Browser page | JSON-serializable key/value data backed by the Cache API | Included in the default web set |
| [URL](./web/url.md) | Browser page | Small, shareable UI state in a query or hash | Register `URLAdapter` explicitly |
| [Preferences](./capacitor/preferences.md) | Capacitor iOS/Android | Native app preferences | Register Capacitor adapters |
| [Secure](./capacitor/secure.md) | Capacitor iOS/Android | Values through Keychain or EncryptedSharedPreferences | Register Capacitor adapters |
| [SQLite](./capacitor/sqlite.md) | Capacitor iOS/Android | Native SQLite-backed key/value data | Register Capacitor adapters |
| [Filesystem](./capacitor/filesystem.md) | Capacitor iOS/Android | One JSON file per key | Register Capacitor adapters |

Browser quota, native storage limits and latency vary by browser, device, data size and operation. The table does not promise a capacity or benchmark. Test the read path on every platform you ship; [device verification](../../guides/platforms/device-verification.md) remains required for native adapters.

## Choose an adapter

`defineStorage()` registers the standard browser set and initializes on first operation. Without an explicit `storage` option, Strata tries the configured `defaultStorages` in order and uses the first available registered adapter. It does not rank adapters by speed, reliability or capacity.

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'Working copy' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');
```

To target a specific adapter, supply its name. A fallback list is tried in your chosen order:

```typescript
await storage.set('draft', { title: 'Working copy' }, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
await storage.set('session-note', 'editing', {
  storage: ['sessionStorage', 'memory'],
});
```

Register native adapters before selecting `preferences`, `secure`, `sqlite` or `filesystem`:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const nativeStorage = defineStorage();
await registerCapacitorAdapters(nativeStorage);
await nativeStorage.set('device-setting', 'on', { storage: 'preferences' });
```

The native example needs a Capacitor runtime and device verification. The Secure adapter uses platform facilities, but Strata's public options do not request biometric authentication or promise hardware-backed keys. Do not treat a browser test as proof of native behaviour.

## Capability boundary

The Strata API exposes key/value operations. Its IndexedDB and SQLite adapters use their underlying storage systems, but Strata does not expose native database transactions, indexes or raw SQL through `storage`. Use a platform API directly when you need those features. The Cache adapter stores serializable values, not `Request`/`Response` objects or service worker request caches; use the browser Cache API directly for those tasks.

`storage.getCapabilities(name)` reports an adapter's declared capabilities after it is registered. Capability flags describe the adapter interface; they do not replace a runtime availability check or a read/write/read test.

For custom adapter implementation and registration, follow the [custom adapters guide](../../guides/advanced/custom-adapters.md). For optional Firebase adapters, follow the [Firebase guide](../../guides/platforms/firebase.md) and select them explicitly after setup.


================================================================================
# Cache Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/cache
================================================================================

# Cache Adapter

Store Strata key-value data in the browser Cache API.

## Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: { cache: { cacheName: 'myapp-data-v1' } },
});

await storage.set('api:/items', { items: ['one', 'two'] }, {
  storage: 'cache',
  ttl: 300_000,
});

const cached = await storage.get<{ items: string[] }>('api:/items', {
  storage: 'cache',
});
```

The adapter uses **string keys and JSON-serializable values**. It serializes data inside Cache API responses; it does not store a `Request` or `Response` as the value you receive from `storage.get()`. Use the browser's Cache API directly when you need HTTP request matching or a `Response` object.

## Availability and behavior

The current adapter requires `window` and `window.caches`. It is available from a supported browser page, not from a service worker global scope. Cache API availability and storage quota depend on the browser and origin. Values expire through Strata's TTL handling; an expired value is not a stale-response fallback.

`StrataConfig.adapters.cache` accepts `cacheName`. Per-call `StorageOptions` does not accept Cache API matching flags such as `ignoreSearch`, `ignoreMethod`, or `ignoreVary`.

```typescript
const keys = await storage.keys(/^api:/, { storage: 'cache' });
for (const key of keys) {
  await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'cache' });
}
```

## See also

- [Offline support example](../../../examples/offline-support.md)
- [TTL guide](../../../guides/features/ttl.md)


================================================================================
# Cookie Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/cookies
================================================================================

# Cookie Adapter

Store small, non-sensitive values in browser cookies.

:::info Shared storage area
The adapter defaults to the `strata_` cookie-name prefix. It lists and clears only values written in Strata's storage envelope. See [key ownership](../../../configuration.md#key-ownership).
:::

## Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: { cookies: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' } },
});

await storage.set('language', 'en', {
  storage: 'cookies',
  ttl: 86_400_000,
});
const language = await storage.get<string>('language', { storage: 'cookies' });
```

`StrataConfig.adapters.cookies` accepts `secure` and `sameSite` (`'strict'`, `'lax'`, or `'none'`). These are instance settings, not options to pass to `set()` or `get()`. Cookie size is limited by the browser; this adapter reports a 4 KB per-cookie limit.

To set a domain or path, create and register a `CookieAdapter` directly:

```typescript
import { Strata, CookieAdapter } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = new Strata({ defaultStorages: ['cookies'] });
storage.registerAdapter(new CookieAdapter('strata_', {
  domain: '.example.com',
  path: '/',
  secure: true,
  sameSite: 'lax',
}));
await storage.initialize();
```

Cookies written by JavaScript cannot be `HttpOnly`, so do not store session secrets with this adapter. If a server needs an `HttpOnly` session cookie, it must send the `Set-Cookie` header itself.

## See also

- [Storage adapters](../README.md)
- [Configuration](../../../configuration.md)


================================================================================
# IndexedDB Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/indexeddb
================================================================================

# IndexedDB Adapter

Store structured key-value data in the browser's IndexedDB database.

## Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: {
    indexedDB: { dbName: 'MyAppDB', version: 1 },
  },
});

await storage.set('draft:123', { title: 'First draft' }, {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
});
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft:123', {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
});
```

`StrataConfig.adapters.indexedDB` accepts `dbName` and `version`. Its store layout is managed by the adapter. It does not accept a custom object-store schema, an upgrade callback, or an `onBlocked` callback.

## Key-value operations

```typescript
await storage.set('draft:124', { title: 'Second draft' }, {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
  ttl: 86_400_000,
});

const draftKeys = await storage.keys(/^draft:/, {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
});

for (const key of draftKeys) {
  const value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
  // Use the value in your application.
}
```

The `Strata` instance exposes no `transaction()` method. Sequential `set()` calls do not make an atomic group. For atomic updates across several records, custom indexes, or blocked-upgrade events, use the browser IndexedDB API directly.

IndexedDB quotas and persistent-storage decisions are browser controlled. Applications can inspect `navigator.storage.estimate()` and request persistence with `navigator.storage.persist()` where supported.

## See also

- [Storage adapters](../README.md)
- [Query guide](../../../guides/features/queries.md)


================================================================================
# LocalStorage Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/localstorage
================================================================================

# LocalStorage Adapter

Persistent browser storage using the localStorage API.

## Overview

The LocalStorage adapter provides simple, synchronous, persistent storage in web browsers. Data persists across browser sessions and page reloads.

### Capabilities

| Feature | Support |
|---------|----------|
| Persistence | ✅ Yes |
| Synchronous | ✅ Yes |
| Observable | ✅ Yes (same origin) |
| Searchable | ✅ Yes |
| Iterable | ✅ Yes |
| Capacity | Varies by browser and available device storage |
| Performance | 🚀 Fast |
| TTL Support | ✅ Yes (manual) |
| Batch Support | ✅ Yes |
| Transaction Support | ❌ No |

## Shared storage areas {#shared-storage-areas}

`localStorage` is shared with every other script on the origin. Since 3.0.0, this adapter prefixes
keys with `strata:` by default. Set `keyPrefix: false` only when another script must read the exact
physical key; older unprefixed keys can migrate on read.

**Since 2.9.0 the adapter identifies its own data by shape**: a key counts as its own only when the
stored value deserializes into a `StorageValue` envelope. Everything else is skipped.

What that means in practice:

- `keys()` returns only keys this library wrote. A key put in `localStorage` by anything else is
  invisible to it **by design**.
- The TTL sweep and `clear()` never read, delete, or log about another application's data.
- A value that is not ours is **not an error** — it is evidence the key belongs to somebody else. It is
  skipped and reported at `debug`. `logger.error` is reserved for a key carrying our own envelope that
  still fails, and for a genuine storage-access fault such as a blocked origin.

```typescript
import { setLogLevel } from 'strata-storage';
setLogLevel('debug');   // names every skipped key and why
```

:::note Before 2.9.0
An empty prefix made the adapter claim every key on the origin. It logged
`Failed to get key <foreign-key> from localStorage: SyntaxError…` on every TTL sweep, returned foreign
keys from `keys()`, and could delete a foreign key whose JSON happened to carry an expired `expires`.
Setting a prefix or a namespace is still good practice for a clean keyspace — it is no longer what keeps
the library off other people's keys.
:::

## Usage

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();

// Explicitly use localStorage
await storage.set('preference', value, { storage: 'localStorage' });
```

## Configuration

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: {
    localStorage: {
      prefix: 'myapp_'
    }
  }
});
```

### Configuration Options

- `prefix` (string): This adapter's physical-key prefix. The instance-level `keyPrefix` defaults to
  `strata:` and can be set to `false` for a known external reader; an adapter prefix overrides it.
  The adapter still identifies its own stored values by their envelope shape.

## Features

### Cross-Tab Synchronization

```typescript
// Changes are synchronized across tabs
storage.subscribe((change) => {
  if (change.source === 'remote') {
    console.log(`Tab updated ${change.key}`);
  }
}, { storage: 'localStorage' });
```

### Domain Persistence

```typescript
// Data persists for the domain
await storage.set('userData', user, { storage: 'localStorage' });
// Available after browser restart
```

### Synchronous Operations

```typescript
// LocalStorage operations are synchronous under the hood
// But Strata wraps them in promises for consistency
const value = await storage.get('key', { storage: 'localStorage' });
```

## Use Cases

### 1. User Preferences

```typescript
class PreferenceManager {
  async saveTheme(theme: 'light' | 'dark') {
    await storage.set('theme', theme, { 
      storage: 'localStorage' 
    });
  }
  
  async getTheme() {
    return await storage.get<'light' | 'dark'>('theme', { 
      storage: 'localStorage' 
    }) || 'light';
  }
  
  async saveLanguage(lang: string) {
    await storage.set('language', lang, { 
      storage: 'localStorage' 
    });
  }
}
```

### 2. Form Draft Saving

```typescript
// Auto-save form drafts
function setupFormAutosave(formId: string) {
  const form = document.getElementById(formId);
  
  form?.addEventListener('input', async (e) => {
    const formData = new FormData(form as HTMLFormElement);
    const data = Object.fromEntries(formData);
    
    await storage.set(`draft:${formId}`, data, {
      storage: 'localStorage',
      ttl: 604800000 // 7 days
    });
  });
  
  // Restore draft on load
  const draft = await storage.get(`draft:${formId}`, {
    storage: 'localStorage'
  });
  
  if (draft) {
    // Restore form fields
  }
}
```

### 3. Shopping Cart

```typescript
class CartManager {
  private cartKey = 'shopping_cart';
  
  async addItem(item: CartItem) {
    const cart = await this.getCart();
    cart.items.push(item);
    cart.updatedAt = Date.now();
    
    await storage.set(this.cartKey, cart, {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async getCart(): Promise<Cart> {
    const cart = await storage.get<Cart>(this.cartKey, {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    });
    
    return cart || { items: [], updatedAt: Date.now() };
  }
  
  async clearCart() {
    await storage.remove(this.cartKey, {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    });
  }
}
```

### 4. Offline Queue

```typescript
// Queue actions for offline processing
class OfflineQueue {
  async addAction(action: Action) {
    const queue = await this.getQueue();
    queue.push({
      ...action,
      timestamp: Date.now()
    });
    
    await storage.set('offline_queue', queue, {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async processQueue() {
    const queue = await this.getQueue();
    
    for (const action of queue) {
      try {
        await this.processAction(action);
        // Remove processed action
      } catch (error) {
        // Keep in queue for retry
      }
    }
  }
  
  private async getQueue() {
    return await storage.get('offline_queue', {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    }) || [];
  }
}
```

## Storage Limits

Browser storage limits vary by browser, device, origin, private-browsing mode,
and current disk space. Treat a quota error as a possible write outcome; do not
design around a fixed per-browser capacity.

### Handling Quota Errors

```typescript
import { QuotaExceededError } from 'strata-storage';

try {
  await storage.set('data', largeData, { storage: 'localStorage' });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) {
    // Only remove data that your application can recreate.
    await storage.clear({
      storage: 'localStorage',
      prefix: 'cache:',
    });
    await storage.set('data', largeData, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Cross-Origin Limitations

```typescript
// LocalStorage is bound to origin (protocol + domain + port)
// https://example.com cannot access http://example.com localStorage
// example.com:3000 cannot access example.com:3001 localStorage

// Use a consistent origin or implement cross-origin communication
if (window.location.origin === 'https://app.example.com') {
  await storage.set('data', value, { storage: 'localStorage' });
}
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Use Prefixes

```typescript
// Namespace your keys to avoid conflicts
const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: {
    localStorage: {
      prefix: 'myapp_v1_'
    }
  }
});
```

### 2. Implement Versioning

```typescript
// Version your storage schema
const STORAGE_VERSION = 2;

async function migrateStorage() {
  const version = await storage.get('_version', { 
    storage: 'localStorage' 
  });
  
  if (!version || version < STORAGE_VERSION) {
    // Run migrations
    if (version === 1) {
      await migrateV1ToV2();
    }
    
    await storage.set('_version', STORAGE_VERSION, { 
      storage: 'localStorage' 
    });
  }
}
```

### 3. Handle Storage Events

```typescript
// Listen for changes from other tabs
window.addEventListener('storage', (e) => {
  if (e.key?.startsWith('myapp_')) {
    console.log('Storage changed:', e.key, e.newValue);
  }
});

// Or use Strata's subscription
const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe((change) => {
  console.log('Change detected:', change);
}, { storage: 'localStorage' });
```

### 4. Compress Large Data

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const compressedStorage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } });
await compressedStorage.set('largeData', data, {
  storage: 'localStorage',
  compress: true,
});
```

Compression runs only when the instance has `compression.enabled: true`; a per-write flag alone does not create the compressor. It may leave a value uncompressed when that value would not get smaller.

## Performance Considerations

### 1. Blocking Operations

```typescript
// localStorage is synchronous and can block the main thread
// For large operations, consider batching

const batch = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
  batch.push({ key: `item_${i}`, value: data[i] });
}

// Batch write
for (const { key, value } of batch) {
  await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'localStorage' });
}
```

### 2. JSON Serialization

```typescript
// Avoid storing non-serializable values
const good = {
  name: 'John',
  age: 30,
  tags: ['user', 'active']
};

const bad = {
  date: new Date(), // Loses type
  func: () => {}, // Cannot serialize
  regex: /pattern/ // Loses type
};

// Adapter-level serialize/deserialize callbacks are not part of StrataConfig.
// Convert a custom value to a supported data shape before calling set().
```

## Security Considerations

### 1. No Sensitive Data

Do not store account passwords in any client-side adapter. Browser `localStorage` is readable by scripts on the origin. A Capacitor app can register the native `secure` adapter for a device-held credential, but that is not a server authentication session or a browser fallback.

### 2. XSS Vulnerabilities

```typescript
// Validate data before storing
function sanitizeUserInput(input: string): string {
  // Remove potential XSS vectors
  return input.replace(/<script[^>]*>.*?<\/script>/gi, '');
}

await storage.set('userContent', sanitizeUserInput(content), {
  storage: 'localStorage'
});
```

## Migration and Fallbacks

```typescript
// Fallback chain when localStorage is not available
await storage.set('data', value, {
  storage: ['localStorage', 'sessionStorage', 'memory']
});

// Check availability
if (storage.getAvailableStorageTypes().includes('localStorage')) {
  // Use localStorage
} else {
  // Use alternative
}
```

## Debugging

```typescript
// Debug localStorage contents
const allKeys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'localStorage' });
for (const key of allKeys) {
  const value = await storage.get(key, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  console.log(key, value);
}

// Get size information
const size = await storage.size(true);
console.log('LocalStorage usage:', size.byStorage?.localStorage);
```

## See Also

- [Storage Adapters Overview](../README.md)
- [SessionStorage Adapter](./sessionstorage.md) - Session-scoped storage
- [IndexedDB Adapter](./indexeddb.md) - Large-scale storage
- [Cross-Tab Sync Guide](../../../guides/features/sync.md)


================================================================================
# Memory adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/memory
================================================================================

# Memory adapter

The memory adapter keeps values in a JavaScript `Map`. Its values disappear when the page or process is reloaded. Use it for data you can regenerate, short-lived previews and tests.

## Use it

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: 'memory' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft', {
  storage: 'memory',
});
```

`defineStorage()` registers memory with the standard browser adapters. A manual `new Strata()` instance needs a registered `MemoryAdapter` before use.

## Configure a limit

```typescript
const limitedStorage = defineStorage({
  adapters: { memory: { maxSize: 50 * 1024 * 1024 } },
});
```

`maxSize` is a configured byte limit, not a default allocation or a measured capacity. A write that exceeds it throws; the adapter does not evict old entries. Without a configured limit, available JavaScript heap memory is the practical boundary.

## Expiry and queries

```typescript
await storage.set('report:1', {
  tags: ['important'],
  score: 85,
}, {
  storage: 'memory',
  ttl: 300_000,
});

const matches = await storage.query<{ tags: string[]; score: number }>({
  tags: { $in: ['important'] },
  score: { $gte: 80 },
}, { storage: 'memory' });
```

`query()` matches the decoded value, not Strata's internal metadata. Its condition field names are fields of the value you stored. See the [query API](../../features/query.md) for operators.

To remove only a key family, use a supported `clear` filter:

```typescript
await storage.clear({ storage: 'memory', prefix: 'report:' });
```

Memory reads and writes are synchronous at the adapter level, and Strata also exposes async methods. Performance depends on value size and the surrounding application; measure the actual workload instead of assuming a fixed latency.

## Limits

- Reloading or restarting clears the adapter.
- A separate tab or process has a separate memory map.
- The adapter has no atomic transaction API and no automatic eviction policy.
- Use a persistent adapter when the value must survive a reload.


================================================================================
# SessionStorage Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/sessionstorage
================================================================================

# SessionStorage Adapter

Session-scoped browser storage using the sessionStorage API.

## Overview

The SessionStorage adapter provides temporary storage that persists for the duration of the browser tab/window session. Data is cleared when the tab is closed.

### Capabilities

| Feature | Support |
|---------|----------|
| Persistence | 🔄 Session only |
| Synchronous | ✅ Yes |
| Observable | ✅ Yes (same-tab changes; no cross-tab sync) |
| Searchable | ✅ Yes |
| Iterable | ✅ Yes |
| Capacity | Varies by browser and available device storage |
| Performance | 🚀 Fast |
| TTL Support | ✅ Yes (manual) |
| Batch Support | ✅ Yes |
| Transaction Support | ❌ No |

:::info Shared storage area — key ownership
This area is shared with every other script on the origin. Since 3.0.0, the adapter prefixes keys with
`strata:` by default. The adapter has also checked the stored `StorageValue` envelope since 2.9.0, so
`keys()`, the TTL sweep and `clear()` never touch data this library did not write. A key written here by
anything else is invisible to `keys()` by design; `setLogLevel('debug')` shows what is being skipped.
Full explanation: [Configuration ▸ key ownership](../../../configuration.md#key-ownership).
:::

## Usage

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();

// Explicitly use sessionStorage
await storage.set('sessionData', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
```

## Configuration

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  adapters: {
    sessionStorage: {
      prefix: 'session_'
    }
  }
});
```

### Configuration Options

- `prefix` (string): Physical key prefix. The instance-level default is `strata:`; this adapter option overrides it. Serialization callbacks are not part of `StrataConfig`.

## Features

### Tab Isolation

```typescript
// Each tab has its own sessionStorage
// Tab 1
await storage.set('tabId', 'tab1', { storage: 'sessionStorage' });

// Tab 2 (different tab)
const tabId = await storage.get('tabId', { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
console.log(tabId); // null - different session
```

### Session Persistence

```typescript
// Data survives page refresh within the same tab
await storage.set('formProgress', { step: 3 }, { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});

// After page refresh (same tab)
const progress = await storage.get('formProgress', { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});
console.log(progress); // { step: 3 }
```

### Automatic Cleanup

```typescript
// No manual cleanup needed - cleared when tab closes
await storage.set('tempData', data, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
// Automatically cleared when user closes the tab
```

## Use Cases

### 1. Multi-Step Forms

```typescript
class FormWizard {
  private currentStep = 1;
  private formKey = 'wizard_data';
  
  async saveStep(stepData: unknown) {
    const existing = await this.getFormData();
    const updated = {
      ...existing,
      [`step${this.currentStep}`]: stepData,
      currentStep: this.currentStep,
      lastUpdated: Date.now()
    };
    
    await storage.set(this.formKey, updated, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async getFormData() {
    return await storage.get(this.formKey, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    }) || {};
  }
  
  async nextStep() {
    this.currentStep++;
    await this.saveStep({ step: this.currentStep });
  }
  
  async submitForm() {
    const formData = await this.getFormData();
    await api.submitForm(formData);
    
    // Clear after submission
    await storage.remove(this.formKey, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
}
```

### 2. Shopping Session

```typescript
class SessionCart {
  async addItem(item: CartItem) {
    const cart = await this.getCart();
    cart.items.push(item);
    cart.sessionId = cart.sessionId || generateSessionId();
    
    await storage.set('session_cart', cart, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async getCart() {
    return await storage.get('session_cart', {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    }) || { items: [], sessionId: null };
  }
  
  async convertToUser(userId: string) {
    const sessionCart = await this.getCart();
    
    // Move to persistent storage
    await storage.set(`cart:${userId}`, sessionCart, {
      storage: 'localStorage'
    });
    
    // Clear session cart
    await storage.remove('session_cart', {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
}
```

### 3. Temporary signed-in page state

Keep only recreatable interface state here, such as the selected tab or an
unfinished search. Let your authentication system manage credentials; a value
in `sessionStorage` is readable by scripts on the page and cannot prove that a
user is signed in.

### 4. Page State Management

```typescript
class PageStateManager {
  async saveScrollPosition(page: string) {
    await storage.set(`scroll:${page}`, {
      x: window.scrollX,
      y: window.scrollY,
      timestamp: Date.now()
    }, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async restoreScrollPosition(page: string) {
    const position = await storage.get(`scroll:${page}`, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
    
    if (position) {
      window.scrollTo(position.x, position.y);
    }
  }
  
  async saveFilters(filters: FilterOptions) {
    await storage.set('page_filters', filters, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
  
  async getFilters() {
    return await storage.get('page_filters', {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
  }
}
```

## Storage Behavior

### Tab Duplication

```typescript
// When duplicating a tab, sessionStorage is copied
// Original tab
await storage.set('data', { value: 1 }, { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});

// Duplicated tab starts with same data
const data = await storage.get('data', { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});
console.log(data); // { value: 1 }

// But changes are independent
await storage.set('data', { value: 2 }, { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});
// Original tab still has { value: 1 }
```

### Navigation Behavior

```typescript
// SessionStorage persists across:
// - Page refresh (F5)
// - Navigation within same origin
// - History back/forward

// SessionStorage is cleared when:
// - Tab is closed
// - Browser is closed
// - New tab is opened (even to same URL)
```

## Best Practices

### 1. Use for Temporary State

```typescript
// Good: Temporary form data
await storage.set('formDraft', draft, { 
  storage: 'sessionStorage' 
});

// Bad: User preferences (use localStorage)
await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { 
  storage: 'localStorage' // Better choice
});
```

### 2. Implement Recovery

```typescript
class SessionManager {
  async getOrCreate(key: string, factory: () => Promise<unknown>) {
    let value = await storage.get(key, { 
      storage: 'sessionStorage' 
    });
    
    if (!value) {
      value = await factory();
      await storage.set(key, value, { 
        storage: 'sessionStorage' 
      });
    }
    
    return value;
  }
}

// Usage
const sessionId = await sessionManager.getOrCreate(
  'sessionId',
  async () => generateSessionId()
);
```

### 3. Clean Up Sensitive Data

```typescript
// Clear recreatable session data explicitly on sign-out.
class SecureSession {
  async logout() {
    await storage.clear({ storage: 'sessionStorage', prefix: 'session_' });
  }
}
```

### 4. Handle Tab Communication

```typescript
// Since sessionStorage doesn't sync between tabs,
// use localStorage or BroadcastChannel for tab communication

class TabCoordinator {
  async setLeaderTab() {
    const tabId = generateTabId();
    
    // Store in session
    await storage.set('tabId', tabId, {
      storage: 'sessionStorage'
    });
    
    // Announce to other tabs via localStorage
    await storage.set('activeTab', tabId, {
      storage: 'localStorage',
      ttl: 5000 // 5 second heartbeat
    });
  }
}
```

## Performance Optimization

### 1. Minimize Storage Size

```typescript
// SessionStorage has same size limits as localStorage
// Keep data compact

interface CompactSession {
  id: string;
  s: number; // start time
  u: number; // last update
  d: unknown; // data
}

// Use short keys for frequently accessed data
await storage.set('s', compactSession, {
  storage: 'sessionStorage'
});
```

### 2. Batch Operations

```typescript
// Batch multiple operations
const updates = [
  { key: 'view1', value: data1 },
  { key: 'view2', value: data2 },
  { key: 'view3', value: data3 }
];

for (const { key, value } of updates) {
  await storage.set(key, value, { 
    storage: 'sessionStorage' 
  });
}
```

## Security Considerations

### 1. Session tokens

Do not treat a browser-stored user agent, origin, or expiry field as proof of a
valid login. The server must validate its own session or access token on every
protected request. Avoid putting reusable credentials in browser storage.

### 2. Data Sensitivity

```typescript
// Be cautious with sensitive data
// SessionStorage is accessible via JavaScript

// Encryption requires a password supplied separately from browser storage.
await storage.set('sensitiveData', data, {
  storage: 'sessionStorage',
  encrypt: true,
  encryptionPassword: sessionKey
});
```

## Comparison with LocalStorage

| Feature | SessionStorage | LocalStorage |
|---------|---------------|---------------|
| Persistence | Tab session | Permanent |
| Sharing | Tab-specific | Domain-wide |
| Capacity | Browser-dependent | Browser-dependent |
| Use Case | Temporary state | User preferences |
| Auto-cleanup | Yes (tab close) | No |

## Migration Strategy

```typescript
// Graceful fallback when sessionStorage unavailable
const sessionFallback = ['sessionStorage', 'memory'];

await storage.set('data', value, {
  storage: sessionFallback
});

// Detect private browsing mode
function hasSessionStorage() {
  try {
    const test = '__test__';
    sessionStorage.setItem(test, test);
    sessionStorage.removeItem(test);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}
```

## See Also

- [Storage Adapters Overview](../README.md)
- [LocalStorage Adapter](./localstorage.md) - Persistent storage
- [Memory Adapter](./memory.md) - Non-persistent alternative


================================================================================
# URL Adapter
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/api/adapters/web/url
================================================================================

# URL Adapter

Persists state in the page URL — shareable, bookmarkable, reload-surviving UI state.

## Overview

The URL adapter (`URLAdapter`, storage type `'url'`) stores each key as a URL parameter, either in the query string (`?strata.tab=pending`) or the hash fragment (`#strata.tab=pending`). It is built for small, serializable UI state that should survive a reload and round-trip through navigation: active tab, filters, pagination, selected entity. Added in `2.5.0`.

URL access is inherently synchronous, so this adapter works with the [synchronous API](../../core/strata.md#synchronous-api). It also listens for `popstate` (query mode) or `hashchange` (hash mode), so back/forward navigation and manual URL edits notify subscribers as `'remote'` changes.

### Capabilities

| Feature | Support |
|---------|---------|
| Persistence | ❌ No (lives only as long as the URL) |
| Synchronous | ✅ Yes |
| Observable | ✅ Yes (`popstate` / `hashchange`) |
| Searchable | ✅ Yes (via key scan) |
| Iterable | ✅ Yes |
| Capacity | ~2 KB practical URL budget |
| Cross-tab | ❌ No |
| Encrypted | ❌ No |
| Transaction Support | ❌ No |

## Usage

The URL adapter is not part of the default web set, so register it explicitly:

```typescript
import { defineStorage, URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
storage.registerAdapter(new URLAdapter());

// Write (no await needed — URL access is synchronous)
storage.setSync('tab', 'pending', { storage: 'url' });
storage.setSync('page', 3, { storage: 'url' });

// Read it back, e.g. on reload
const tab = storage.getSync<string>('tab', { storage: 'url' });

// The async API works too and delegates to the synchronous core
await storage.set('q', 'invoices', { storage: 'url' });
```

## Configuration

Configure the adapter directly before registering it. `StrataConfig.adapters` has no `url` field.

```typescript
import { URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
const url = new URLAdapter();
url.configure({ mode: 'hash', history: 'push' });
storage.registerAdapter(url);
```

### Configuration Options

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
|--------|------|---------|---------|
| `mode` | `'query'` \| `'hash'` | `'query'` | Store params in the query string or the hash fragment. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `'strata.'` | Prefix on every param name to avoid collisions with your own query params. |
| `history` | `'push'` \| `'replace'` | `'replace'` | Add a browser history entry per write, or replace the current entry. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | `2000` | Soft warning threshold (chars) for total URL length. |

## Features

### Reacting to navigation

The adapter emits change events when the URL changes from outside your code — browser back/forward, or a user editing the address bar. Subscribe to react to those changes:

```typescript
storage.subscribe((change) => {
  if (change.key === 'tab') applyTab(change.newValue);
}, { storage: 'url' });
```

### Query vs hash mode

Query mode (`?strata.tab=...`) is shared with the server on every navigation and works well for SSR-readable state. Hash mode (`#strata.tab=...`) keeps state entirely client-side — the fragment is never sent to the server.

```typescript
import { defineStorage, URLAdapter } from 'strata-storage';

// Choose one mode for an instance. Query is the default.
const queryStorage = defineStorage();
queryStorage.registerAdapter(new URLAdapter());

// For fragment state, configure a separate adapter before registration.
const hashStorage = defineStorage();
const hashAdapter = new URLAdapter();
hashAdapter.configure({ mode: 'hash' });
hashStorage.registerAdapter(hashAdapter);
```

## Use Cases

### 1. Shareable list filters

```typescript
function applyFilter(status: string, page: number) {
  storage.setSync('status', status, { storage: 'url' });
  storage.setSync('page', page, { storage: 'url' });
}

// On load, restore the filters from the URL so a shared link reproduces the view
const status = storage.getSync<string>('status', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 'all';
const page = storage.getSync<number>('page', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 1;
```

### 2. Active tab that survives reload

```typescript
function selectTab(tab: string) {
  storage.setSync('tab', tab, { storage: 'url' });
}

window.addEventListener('load', () => {
  selectTab(storage.getSync<string>('tab', { storage: 'url' }) ?? 'overview');
});
```

## Limitations

Documented honestly so you choose the right backend:

- **Length limits.** URLs have practical limits (~2000 chars in some browsers and servers). This adapter is for small, simple, serializable state — not bulk data. Writes past `maxLength` are still performed but logged as a debug warning suggesting a different storage.
- **Server visibility.** In `'query'` mode the data is sent to the server on every navigation and appears in server/proxy/referrer logs. Use `'hash'` mode for client-only state. Never store secrets in the URL in either mode.
- **Browser only.** Outside a browser (SSR/Node), `isAvailable()` returns `false` and the adapter is skipped.
- **Not durable.** State lives only as long as the URL does. It is not persistent storage — pair with `localStorage`/IndexedDB if the value must outlive the URL.
- **No encryption/compression.** Like all backends, encrypt/compress require the async path; for the URL adapter, storing large or sensitive values is discouraged regardless.

## See Also

- [Storage Adapters Overview](../README.md)
- [Synchronous API](../../core/strata.md#synchronous-api) — read/write the URL without `await`
- [LocalStorage Adapter](./localstorage.md) — durable client-only storage
- [Cookie Adapter](./cookies.md) — small server-readable storage
