# Moving from capacitor-secure-storage-plugin to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/capacitor-secure-storage-plugin
================================================================================

# Moving from capacitor-secure-storage-plugin

This plugin does one job: string secrets in the Keychain and in Keystore-backed preferences. If that's all your app stores, keep it. Switch when the secure store sits beside others and you want one call shape for all of them.

## Unwrapping `{ value }`

| capacitor-secure-storage-plugin | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `SecureStoragePlugin.set({ key, value })` | `storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'secure' })` |
| `SecureStoragePlugin.get({ key })` returns `{ value }` | `storage.get(key, { storage: 'secure' })` returns the value |
| `SecureStoragePlugin.remove({ key })` | `storage.remove(key, { storage: 'secure' })` |
| `SecureStoragePlugin.keys()` returns `{ value }` | `storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'secure' })` returns the array |
| `SecureStoragePlugin.clear()` | `storage.clear({ storage: 'secure' })` |

`get()` on a missing key returns `null` here. If your code catches a rejection from the plugin to detect a missing key, change that check.

## Copy on the device

```ts
import { SecureStoragePlugin } from 'capacitor-secure-storage-plugin';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

export const storage = defineStorage();

export async function moveSecrets(): Promise<void> {
  await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:secure-plugin', { storage: 'secure' })) return;
  const { value: keys } = await SecureStoragePlugin.keys();
  for (const key of keys) {
    const { value } = await SecureStoragePlugin.get({ key });
    await storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'secure' });
  }
  await storage.set('moved:secure-plugin', true, { storage: 'secure' });
}
```

Don't log these values while you test the copy. Run `npx cap sync` after installing, or the native module never reaches your projects.

## Limits to read first

The `secure` adapter doesn't expose Keychain accessibility, a biometric requirement or an authentication prompt ([secure adapter](../api/adapters/capacitor/secure.md)). It's native only, too. A browser run won't exercise it, so check the read on [each device](../guides/platforms/device-verification.md), and only then remove the plugin's entries with `SecureStoragePlugin.clear()`, in a later release.

## The plugin, per its README

From the README and npm entry, 7 Nov 2026. Five rows read "Not stated on the pages we checked": the plugin's pages don't raise them, which tells you nothing about whether it could. [Check capacitor-secure-storage-plugin yourself](https://github.com/martinkasa/capacitor-secure-storage-plugin), or open the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/capacitor-secure-storage-plugin).

|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Partly. On the web values go to localStorage base64-encoded; the README says the browser has no secure storage ([source](https://github.com/martinkasa/capacitor-secure-storage-plugin/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| IndexedDB | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| sessionStorage | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| Cookies | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| URL parameters as a store | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| iOS Keychain | Yes ([source](https://github.com/martinkasa/capacitor-secure-storage-plugin/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

# Moving from Dexie.js to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/dexie
================================================================================

# Moving from Dexie.js

Dexie.js is a database: versioned schemas, indexes, bulk writes, live queries. Strata Storage is a key-value layer. If your queries lean on indexes or your tables hold many thousands of rows, stay on Dexie: `storage.query()` reads and decodes every key in the store rather than using an index. This guide fits a smaller case, where Dexie ended up holding settings, drafts and caches and you also need native stores.

## From table calls to keys

| Dexie.js | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `db.table('drafts').put(row)` | `storage.set('draft:' + row.id, row)` |
| `db.table('drafts').get(id)` | `storage.get('draft:' + id)` |
| `db.table('drafts').delete(id)` | `storage.remove('draft:' + id)` |
| `db.table('drafts').where(...)` | `storage.query({ type: 'draft', ... })` |
| `liveQuery(...)` | `storage.subscribe(callback)` |
| `db.version(n).stores(...)` | No equivalent: there's no schema |

Queries match fields on the value you stored, not its key or tags, so a `type` field on each value is how you select one kind of record ([query guide](../guides/features/queries.md)).

## Copy one table

```ts
import Dexie from 'dexie';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

interface Draft {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  updatedAt: number;
}

const db = new Dexie('app');
db.version(1).stores({ drafts: 'id,updatedAt' });

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'memory'] });

export async function moveDrafts(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:dexie-drafts')) return;
  const rows = await db.table<Draft, number>('drafts').toArray();
  for (const row of rows) {
    await storage.set(`draft:${row.id}`, { ...row, type: 'draft' }, { tags: ['drafts'] });
  }
  await storage.set('moved:dexie-drafts', true);
}
```

## Reading it back

```ts
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'memory'] });
const weekAgo = Date.now() - 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;

const recent = await storage.query<{ title: string }>({ type: 'draft', updatedAt: { $gt: weekAgo } });
console.log(recent.map(({ key, value }) => `${key}: ${value.title}`));

await storage.clear({ tags: ['drafts'] });
```

Results aren't sorted by an index, so sort them yourself. Time a query against a realistic amount of your data before you delete the Dexie code.

## Dexie.js, from its own pages

As of 7 Nov 2026, Dexie's README and npm entry confirm IndexedDB and no runtime dependencies. They don't mention localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, the URL, the Keychain, Android secure storage, native preferences or a single API over web and native stores, so those rows aren't shown. A page staying quiet on something isn't the same as the library lacking it: [Check Dexie.js yourself](https://dexie.org), or open the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/dexie).

| Store or capability | Dexie.js | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| IndexedDB | Yes ([source](https://github.com/dexie/Dexie.js/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/dexie/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | Dexie.js | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | Apache-2.0 ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/dexie/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 4.4.7 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 31,094 bytes gzipped, 97,946 minified, version 4.4.7, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=dexie)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 3,400,609, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/dexie)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving from idb-keyval to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/idb-keyval
================================================================================

# Moving from idb-keyval

idb-keyval is a fraction of Strata Storage's size (the figures are below). If IndexedDB key-value is all you need, keep it. The case for moving is expiry, encryption or cross-tab sync you'd otherwise write around it yourself, or values that also have to reach a native store.

## Same verbs, one extra option

| idb-keyval | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `set(key, value)` | `storage.set(key, value, { storage: 'indexedDB' })` |
| `get(key)` | `storage.get(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' })` |
| `del(key)` | `storage.remove(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' })` |
| `keys()` | `storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'indexedDB' })` |
| `clear()` | `storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB' })` |
| `createStore(db, store)` | `defineStorage({ adapters: { indexedDB: { dbName } } })` |

`defaultStorages: ['indexedDB']` saves you repeating the `storage` option on each call. `setMany`, `getMany` and `update` have no direct equivalent: loop over `set()` and `get()`.

## Carry existing entries over

idb-keyval accepts any valid IndexedDB key: numbers, dates and arrays as well as strings. Strata keys are strings, so decide what the others become. This keeps strings and turns numbers into strings.

```ts
import { entries } from 'idb-keyval';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'memory'] });

export async function moveFromIdbKeyval(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:idb-keyval')) return;
  for (const [key, value] of await entries()) {
    if (typeof key === 'string' || typeof key === 'number') {
      await storage.set(String(key), value);
    }
  }
  await storage.set('moved:idb-keyval', true);
}
```

## What you take on

You're trading 805 bytes for a larger package; the table below has both measurements. Features such as [TTL](../guides/features/ttl.md) and [encryption](../guides/features/encryption.md) are off until you ask for them, so a plain `set()` behaves as it did.

Delete the old database with idb-keyval's `clear()` in a later release, after you've read real keys back.

## idb-keyval, as its README puts it

Checked 7 Nov 2026. idb-keyval's README covers IndexedDB and its npm entry lists no dependencies. Nothing there mentions localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, the URL, any native store, or one API across web and native, so those eight rows are left out. [Check idb-keyval yourself](https://github.com/jakearchibald/idb-keyval) to confirm; the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/idb-keyval) has both libraries in full.

| Store or capability | idb-keyval | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| IndexedDB | Yes ([source](https://github.com/jakearchibald/idb-keyval/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/idb-keyval/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | idb-keyval | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | Apache-2.0 ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/idb-keyval/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 6.3.0 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 805 bytes gzipped, 2,132 minified, version 6.3.0, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=idb-keyval)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 15,406,746, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/idb-keyval)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |


================================================================================
# Moving from idb to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/idb
================================================================================

# Moving from idb

idb is IndexedDB with promises: object stores, indexes, cursors and transactions stay in your hands. Strata hides all of those, so if you use them on purpose, this is the wrong move. It fits when you only ever call `get` and `put`, and you don't want to think in IndexedDB terms or you need the value elsewhere too.

## Store and key become one string

| idb | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `db.put('drafts', value, key)` | `storage.set('drafts:' + key, value)` |
| `db.get('drafts', key)` | `storage.get('drafts:' + key)` |
| `db.delete('drafts', key)` | `storage.remove('drafts:' + key)` |
| `db.getAllKeys('drafts')` | `storage.keys(/^drafts:/)` |
| `db.getFromIndex(...)` | `storage.query({ field: value })`, a scan with no index |
| `db.transaction(...)` | No equivalent: each call stands alone |
| `upgrade()` in `openDB` | Not needed: there's no schema to version |

If two writes must succeed or fail together, keep idb for that data. The prefix on the key is there because Strata has one key space per adapter rather than named object stores; [`namespace`](../configuration.md) is the other way to separate them.

## Copy one object store

```ts
import { openDB } from 'idb';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'memory'] });

export async function moveDrafts(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:idb-drafts')) return;
  const db = await openDB('app');
  for (const key of await db.getAllKeys('drafts')) {
    await storage.set(`drafts:${String(key)}`, await db.get('drafts', key));
  }
  db.close();
  await storage.set('moved:idb-drafts', true);
}
```

Calling `openDB` with no version opens the database as it stands and runs no upgrade. Strata's own database has a different name, so yours is left alone until you call `deleteDB` from idb, in a later release, after real keys have read back correctly.

## What idb documents

We read idb's README and npm entry on 7 Nov 2026. They describe IndexedDB, with no runtime dependencies, and stop there. Other web stores, the URL, the native stores and a shared web-and-native API don't come up, so those rows are gone from this table. [Check idb yourself](https://github.com/jakearchibald/idb), or compare on the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/idb).

| Store or capability | idb | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| IndexedDB | Yes ([source](https://github.com/jakearchibald/idb/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/idb/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | idb | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | ISC ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/idb/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 8.0.4 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 1,493 bytes gzipped, 3,650 minified, version 8.0.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=idb)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 36,224,449, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/idb)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare
================================================================================

# Moving to Strata Storage

Each guide below maps a library's calls to `storage.set()` and friends, shows how to copy the data you already have, and says when you shouldn't move at all. Several of these libraries are the better choice for a narrower job.

All of them follow the same order: install Strata beside the old library, copy once behind a flag, read real keys back, then remove the old library in a later release so a rollback still finds its data.

| Library | What it is | Last checked |
|---|---|---|
| [localForage](./localforage.md) | An async key-value store for browsers that writes to IndexedDB or WebSQL and falls back to localStorage, with a localStorage-shaped API. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [idb-keyval](./idb-keyval.md) | A very small promise-based key-value store on top of IndexedDB, with get, set, del and a few batch helpers. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [Dexie.js](./dexie.md) | A wrapper library for IndexedDB with a schema, queries and bulk operations, plus an optional paid sync service called Dexie Cloud. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [store2](./store2.md) | A small wrapper over localStorage and sessionStorage that adds JSON handling, namespaces and a page-lifetime area. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [@capacitor/preferences](./capacitor-preferences.md) | The official Capacitor plugin for a small string key-value store, backed by UserDefaults on iOS, SharedPreferences on Android and localStorage on the web. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [capacitor-secure-storage-plugin](./capacitor-secure-storage-plugin.md) | A community Capacitor plugin for storing string secrets in the iOS Keychain and Android Keystore-backed SharedPreferences. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [@aparajita/capacitor-secure-storage](./aparajita-capacitor-secure-storage.md) | A Capacitor 8 plugin for secure key-value storage of JSON data in the iOS Keychain (with optional iCloud Keychain sync) and AES-GCM encrypted SharedPreferences on Android. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [@capacitor-community/sqlite](./capacitor-community-sqlite.md) | A community Capacitor plugin for native and Electron SQLite databases, with SQLCipher encryption on native and a web layer through jeep-sqlite. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [@ionic/storage](./ionic-storage.md) | Ionic's key-value storage helper built on localForage: IndexedDB and localStorage out of the box, SQLite through an extra driver, encryption through Ionic Secure Storage. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [idb](./idb.md) | A small library that mirrors the IndexedDB API with promises and usability fixes, for modern browsers. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [unstorage](./unstorage.md) | A universal key-value layer from UnJS with mountable drivers for memory, filesystem, browser storage, Capacitor Preferences, databases and cloud object stores. | 7 Nov 2026 |
| [js-cookie](./js-cookie.md) | A small client-side JavaScript API for reading, writing and deleting cookies with their attributes. | 7 Nov 2026 |

The facts in each guide come from that library's own pages and the npm registry, with a source and date beside each one. The [comparison pages](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare) on the main site put the same facts side by side.

# Moving from @ionic/storage to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/ionic-storage
================================================================================

# Moving from @ionic/storage

`@ionic/storage` sits on localForage and has the same key-value shape, so the calls map one to one. If you're on Ionic with its Angular module and plan to use Ionic Secure Storage, staying is reasonable. Strata makes more sense if you'd rather get encryption and native stores from one package, with no drivers to add.

## One-to-one, apart from `create()`

| @ionic/storage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `await store.create()` | Not needed: the instance starts on first use |
| `store.set(key, value)` | `storage.set(key, value)` |
| `store.get(key)` | `storage.get(key)` |
| `store.remove(key)` | `storage.remove(key)` |
| `store.keys()` | `storage.keys()` |
| `store.clear()` | `storage.clear()` |
| `store.forEach(fn)` | `keys()` and `get()` in a loop |
| `store.length()` | `(await storage.keys()).length` |
| `defineDriver(CordovaSQLiteDriver)` | `registerCapacitorAdapters(storage)` |

## Copy the existing keys

```ts
import { Storage } from '@ionic/storage';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'] });

export async function moveFromIonicStorage(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:ionic-storage')) return;
  const old = new Storage();
  await old.create();
  for (const key of await old.keys()) {
    await storage.set(key, await old.get(key));
  }
  await storage.set('moved:ionic-storage', true);
}
```

If you configured a custom `name`, `storeName` or `driverOrder`, pass the same options to `new Storage()`, or you'll open an empty store and copy nothing. Run this inside the app on the device, because that's where the old data lives.

## Native stores and encryption

On a native build, register the adapters and pick `sqlite`, `preferences` or `secure` per call ([Capacitor setup](../migration.md#capacitor-setup)). Encryption is part of the package and off by default: `{ encrypt: true }` on a `set()`, with a password in the instance's `encryption` config ([encryption guide](../guides/features/encryption.md)). It's a different format from Ionic Secure Storage, so anything encrypted there has to be read through that product first.

## Read from @ionic/storage's README

As read on 7 Nov 2026. The README and npm entry cover localStorage, IndexedDB, the driver-based API and the localforage dependency. They don't mention sessionStorage, cookies, the URL, the Keychain, Android secure storage or native preferences, so those rows are left out. [Check @ionic/storage yourself](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-storage), or compare them on the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/ionic-storage).

| Store or capability | @ionic/storage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Yes ([source](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-storage/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| IndexedDB | Yes ([source](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-storage/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| Web and native stores behind one API | Partly. One API with a driver order; native SQLite needs a separately installed Cordova driver or Ionic Secure Storage ([source](https://github.com/ionic-team/ionic-storage/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | No. Depends on localforage ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/@ionic/storage/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | @ionic/storage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/@ionic/storage/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 4.0.0 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 9,446 bytes gzipped, 31,037 minified, version 4.0.0, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=@ionic/storage)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 133,551, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/@ionic/storage)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving from js-cookie to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/js-cookie
================================================================================

# Moving from js-cookie

Read this before you change anything: Strata's cookie adapter stores a JSON envelope under a `strata_` prefix, not your bare value. A server, or any other script reading `theme=dark`, won't find it. Cookies that anything else reads should stay on js-cookie. Move only the ones your client code alone reads.

## Each js-cookie call, and its Strata form

| js-cookie | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `Cookies.set(name, value)` | `storage.set(name, value, { storage: 'cookies' })` |
| `Cookies.get(name)` | `storage.get(name, { storage: 'cookies' })` |
| `Cookies.remove(name)` | `storage.remove(name, { storage: 'cookies' })` |
| `Cookies.set(name, value, { expires: 7 })` | `storage.set(name, value, { storage: 'cookies', ttl: 7 * 86_400_000 })` |
| `{ secure, sameSite }` | `adapters: { cookies: { secure, sameSite } }`, set once on the instance |
| `{ domain, path }` | `new CookieAdapter('strata_', { domain, path })` ([cookie adapter](../api/adapters/web/cookies.md)) |

js-cookie's `expires` counts days; `ttl` counts milliseconds. `secure` and `sameSite` aren't per-call options here.

## Move named cookies

`Cookies.get()` returns every cookie the page can see, including ones you don't own, so list yours by name.

```ts
import Cookies from 'js-cookie';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ adapters: { cookies: { secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' } } });

const OURS = ['theme', 'language'];

export async function moveCookies(): Promise<void> {
  for (const name of OURS) {
    const value = Cookies.get(name);
    if (value === undefined) continue;
    await storage.set(name, value, { storage: 'cookies', ttl: 30 * 86_400_000 });
    Cookies.remove(name);
  }
}
```

js-cookie doesn't report a cookie's expiry, so the copy has to choose one. Removing the old cookie in the same pass makes the loop safe to repeat. If you set a `path` or `domain` when writing it, pass the same ones to `Cookies.remove`, or the old cookie survives.

The adapter reports a 4 KB per-cookie limit, and the envelope takes some of it, so try your longest value. JavaScript can't write `HttpOnly` cookies with either library, and session secrets don't belong in these.

## js-cookie on paper

Checked 7 Nov 2026. js-cookie's README is about cookies and nothing else, so it says nothing on localStorage, IndexedDB, sessionStorage, the URL, native stores or one API across web and native. We've dropped those rows rather than fill them with "not stated". [Check js-cookie yourself](https://github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie), or see the two side by side on the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/js-cookie).

| Store or capability | js-cookie | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Cookies | Yes ([source](https://github.com/js-cookie/js-cookie/blob/main/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/js-cookie/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | js-cookie | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/js-cookie/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 3.0.8 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 803 bytes gzipped, 1,574 minified, version 3.0.8, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=js-cookie)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 44,197,779, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/js-cookie)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving from localForage to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/localforage
================================================================================

# Moving from localForage

localForage and Strata Storage both give you async key-value calls over IndexedDB. If your app only ever runs in a browser and you're happy with localForage, there's no reason to move. It starts to pay off once the same code also ships under Capacitor, or you want `sessionStorage`, cookies or the URL behind the same call.

## localForage calls, renamed

| localForage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `localforage.setItem(key, value)` | `storage.set(key, value)` |
| `localforage.getItem(key)` | `storage.get(key)` |
| `localforage.removeItem(key)` | `storage.remove(key)` |
| `localforage.keys()` | `storage.keys()` |
| `localforage.clear()` | `storage.clear()` |
| `localforage.config({ driver })` | `defineStorage({ defaultStorages })` |

There's no `iterate()`: call `keys()` and `get()` in a loop, or use [`query()`](../guides/features/queries.md) when you're filtering on a field of the value.

## Carry existing values over

The two libraries don't share a database. Strata's IndexedDB adapter opens its own (`StrataStorage` unless you configure `dbName`), so existing values have to be copied once. Run this at startup before anything reads the moved keys.

```ts
import localforage from 'localforage';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'] });

export async function moveFromLocalForage(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:localforage')) return;
  for (const key of await localforage.keys()) {
    await storage.set(key, await localforage.getItem(key));
  }
  await storage.set('moved:localforage', true);
}
```

The flag goes last, so a tab closed halfway repeats the copy on the next start instead of skipping what's left.

## Before you clear the old store

Read a few real keys back through `storage.get()`. If you keep `Blob` values, read one of those too: IndexedDB can hold it, but a `localStorage` fallback can't. Once you're satisfied, ship `await localforage.clear()` in a later release, so a rollback still finds its data.

Adding native stores is a separate step: see [Capacitor setup](../migration.md#capacitor-setup) and check the read on a [device](../guides/platforms/device-verification.md).

## What localForage's pages say

Read on 7 Nov 2026, from localForage's README and its npm entry. Neither says anything about sessionStorage, cookies, the URL, the iOS Keychain, Android secure storage or native preferences, so those rows are left out; Strata has an adapter for each. That silence isn't proof the library can't do them. [Check localForage yourself](https://github.com/localForage/localForage) to confirm, or compare on the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/localforage).

| Store or capability | localForage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Yes ([source](https://github.com/localForage/localForage/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| IndexedDB | Yes ([source](https://github.com/localForage/localForage/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| Web and native stores behind one API | No. The README says it is designed to run in the browser; no native store is described ([source](https://github.com/localForage/localForage/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | No. Depends on lie ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/localforage/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | localForage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | Apache-2.0 ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/localforage/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 1.10.0 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 8,680 bytes gzipped, 28,346 minified, version 1.10.0, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=localforage)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 11,046,386, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/localforage)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving from store2 to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/store2
================================================================================

# Moving from store2

store2 is synchronous and so are Strata's `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` calls, so most of this is a rename. For a site that only touches those two areas, store2 is the smaller package and a move buys you nothing. The move earns its keep only when values also need IndexedDB, a cookie, the URL or a native store.

## The rename, call by call

| store2 | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `store.set(key, value)` | `storage.setSync(key, value, { storage: 'localStorage' })` |
| `store.get(key)` | `storage.getSync(key, { storage: 'localStorage' })` |
| `store.remove(key)` | `storage.removeSync(key, { storage: 'localStorage' })` |
| `store.has(key)` | `storage.hasSync(key, { storage: 'localStorage' })` |
| `store.keys()` | `storage.keysSync(undefined, { storage: 'localStorage' })` |
| `store.session.set(key, value)` | `storage.setSync(key, value, { storage: 'sessionStorage' })` |
| `store.namespace('cart').set(key, value)` | `storage.setSync(key, value, { storage: 'localStorage', namespace: 'cart' })` |

The sync calls can't encrypt or compress. Those need the async `set()` and `get()`.

## Copy what's there

store2 keeps plain JSON strings under your key. Strata writes under a `strata:` prefix inside its own envelope, so the two can share `localStorage` while you copy. `store.getAll()` sees every key in the area, including Strata's, so skip those.

```ts
import store from 'store2';
import { DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX, defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['localStorage', 'memory'] });

export function moveFromStore2(): void {
  if (storage.getSync<boolean>('moved:store2')) return;
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(store.getAll())) {
    if (!key.startsWith(DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX)) storage.setSync(key, value);
  }
  storage.setSync('moved:store2', true);
}
```

Your old keys stay in place until you remove them, and other code may own some of them, so list the ones you're deleting by name. [Key ownership](../configuration.md#key-ownership) explains what Strata will and won't touch.

If you'd rather move one raw value and drop the original in the same step, `storage.importRawSync('theme', 'theme', { storage: 'localStorage' })` does that, but it keeps the raw string, so you'd call `JSON.parse` on what comes back.

## store2's own description

From store2's README and npm entry, read 7 Nov 2026: localStorage, sessionStorage, and no runtime dependencies. They don't mention IndexedDB, cookies, the URL, native stores or one API across web and native, so those rows are hidden here. Not mentioned isn't the same as missing. [Check store2 yourself](https://github.com/nbubna/store), or open the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/store2).

| Store or capability | store2 | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Yes ([source](https://github.com/nbubna/store/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| sessionStorage | Yes ([source](https://github.com/nbubna/store/blob/master/README.md), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/store2/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | store2 | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Licence | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/store2/latest)) | MIT ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/strata-storage/latest)) |
| npm version | 2.14.4 | 3.1.4 |
| Bundle size | 1,645 bytes gzipped, 4,503 minified, version 2.14.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=store2)) | 21,468 bytes gzipped, 79,645 minified, version 3.1.4, 7 Nov 2026 ([source](https://bundlephobia.com/api/size?package=strata-storage)) |
| Weekly downloads | 2,773,240, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/store2)) | 486, 31 Oct 2026 to 6 Nov 2026 ([source](https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/strata-storage)) |

# Moving from unstorage to Strata Storage
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/compare/unstorage
================================================================================

# Moving from unstorage

Stay on unstorage if the same code runs on servers or edge runtimes, or you mount Redis, S3 or Cloudflare KV. Strata has no server drivers and doesn't try to. Strata is for storage that lives entirely on the device, where you want the Keychain, Android encrypted preferences, SQLite, cookies or the URL.

## Mostly the same names

| unstorage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|
| `store.setItem(key, value)` | `storage.set(key, value)` |
| `store.getItem(key)` | `storage.get(key)` |
| `store.hasItem(key)` | `storage.has(key)` |
| `store.removeItem(key)` | `storage.remove(key)` |
| `store.getKeys()` | `storage.keys()` |
| `store.clear()` | `storage.clear()` |
| `store.watch(callback)` | `storage.subscribe(callback)` |
| `driver: localStorageDriver()` | `{ storage: 'localStorage' }` |
| `driver: indexedDbDriver()` | `{ storage: 'indexedDB' }` |
| `store.mount('prefs', driver)` | `{ storage: 'preferences' }` on the calls that need it |

Instead of mounting a driver at a path, you name the adapter on the call, or set the order once with `defaultStorages`.

## Copying across drivers

```ts
import { createStorage } from 'unstorage';
import localStorageDriver from 'unstorage/drivers/localstorage';
import { DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX, defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const storage = defineStorage({ defaultStorages: ['localStorage', 'memory'] });

export async function moveFromUnstorage(): Promise<void> {
  if (await storage.get<boolean>('moved:unstorage')) return;
  const old = createStorage({ driver: localStorageDriver({}) });
  for (const key of await old.getKeys()) {
    if (!key.startsWith(DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX)) await storage.set(key, await old.getItem(key));
  }
  await storage.set('moved:unstorage', true);
}
```

The prefix check stops the copy picking up Strata's own entries when both libraries share `localStorage`. unstorage normalises separators to `:`, so a key written as `a/b` comes through as `a:b`. Update any code that builds those keys by hand.

Set a `base` on the old driver if you used one, or you'll list keys outside your own area. Read real keys back before you remove them.

## unstorage's drivers, as documented

We read the drivers list, the guide and the npm entry on 7 Nov 2026. Four rows aren't covered by those pages and say so; that's a gap in what's written, not a verdict. [Check unstorage yourself](https://unstorage.unjs.io), or see both on the [side-by-side page](https://stratastorage.aoneahsan.com/compare/unstorage).

| Store or capability | unstorage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|
| localStorage | Yes ([source](https://unstorage.unjs.io/drivers), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| IndexedDB | Yes. Through idb-keyval ([source](https://unstorage.unjs.io/drivers), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| sessionStorage | Yes ([source](https://unstorage.unjs.io/drivers), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| Cookies | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| URL parameters as a store | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| iOS Keychain | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| Android secure storage (Keystore-backed) | Not stated on the pages we checked | Yes |
| Native preferences (UserDefaults / SharedPreferences) | Yes. Requires installing @capacitor/preferences separately ([source](https://unstorage.unjs.io/drivers/capacitor-preferences), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| Web and native stores behind one API | Yes. Drivers are mounted on one storage instance; the native driver covers preferences only ([source](https://unstorage.unjs.io/guide), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |
| No runtime dependencies | Yes. No dependencies field; each driver's backend package is installed by you ([source](https://registry.npmjs.org/unstorage/latest), 7 Nov 2026) | Yes |

| Package fact | unstorage | Strata Storage |
|---|---|---|

# Configuration
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/configuration
================================================================================

# Configuration

Strata Storage provides extensive configuration options to customize behavior for your specific needs.

## Configuration Overview

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  // Platform detection (auto-detected by default)
  platform: 'web', // 'web' | 'ios' | 'android' | 'node'
  
  // Default storage types in order of preference
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
  
  // Storage adapter specific configurations
  adapters: {
    indexedDB: {
      dbName: 'MyAppDB',
      version: 1
    },
    localStorage: {
      prefix: 'myapp_'
    },
    cookies: {
      secure: true,
      sameSite: 'strict'
    }
  },
  
  // Encryption settings
  encryption: {
    enabled: false,
    password: 'your-secure-password',
    algorithm: 'AES-GCM',
    keyLength: 256,
    keyDerivation: 'PBKDF2'
  },
  
  // Compression settings
  compression: {
    enabled: false,
    algorithm: 'lz', // the only supported algorithm
    threshold: 1024  // bytes
  },
  
  // Synchronization settings
  sync: {
    enabled: false,
    storages: ['localStorage'],
    conflictResolution: 'latest'
  },
  
  // Time-to-live settings
  ttl: {
    defaultTTL: 3600000, // 1 hour (ms)
    cleanupInterval: 60000, // 1 minute
    autoCleanup: true
  }
});
```

## Configuration Options

### Platform

Strata automatically detects the platform, but you can override it:

```typescript
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  platform: 'ios' // Force iOS behavior
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
```

`platform` alone does not register native adapters. Run this in a Capacitor app on a device.

**Options:**
- `'web'` - Browser environment
- `'ios'` - iOS native (Capacitor)
- `'android'` - Android native (Capacitor)
- `'node'` - Node.js environment

### Default Storages

Specify storage preference order. Strata will use the first available:

```typescript
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory']
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
```

Register native adapters before reading or writing to `sqlite` or `preferences` on a device.

**Web Options:**
- `'memory'` - In-memory storage
- `'localStorage'` - Browser localStorage
- `'sessionStorage'` - Browser sessionStorage
- `'indexedDB'` - IndexedDB database
- `'cookies'` - HTTP cookies
- `'cache'` - Cache API

**Mobile Options:**
- `'preferences'` - Native preferences (UserDefaults/SharedPreferences)
- `'sqlite'` - SQLite database
- `'secure'` - Keychain (iOS) / EncryptedSharedPreferences (Android)
- `'filesystem'` - File system storage

### Adapter Configuration

#### IndexedDB

```typescript
adapters: {
  indexedDB: {
    dbName: 'MyDatabase',    // Database name
    version: 1               // Database version
  }
}
```

#### LocalStorage/SessionStorage

```typescript
adapters: {
  localStorage: {
    prefix: 'app_'           // Key prefix
  }
}
```

#### Cookies

```typescript
adapters: {
  cookies: {
    secure: true,            // HTTPS only
    sameSite: 'lax'          // 'strict' | 'lax' | 'none'
  }
}
```

#### SQLite (Mobile)

```typescript
adapters: {
  sqlite: {
    filename: 'app.db'       // Database file name
  }
}
```

> The native SQLite backend also accepts per-call `database` / `table` options
> (passed to `get`/`set`/etc.) to address multiple physical stores — see the
> SQLite adapter reference.

### Encryption Configuration

```typescript
encryption: {
  enabled: true,             // Enable/disable encryption
  password: 'secret',        // Encryption password
  algorithm: 'AES-GCM',      // 'AES-GCM' | 'AES-CBC'
  keyLength: 256,            // 128 | 192 | 256
  keyDerivation: 'PBKDF2',   // PBKDF2
  iterations: 600000,        // PBKDF2 iterations (default: 600000, OWASP)
  saltLength: 16             // Salt length in bytes
}
```

### Compression Configuration

```typescript
compression: {
  enabled: true,            // Enable/disable compression
  algorithm: 'lz',          // only the bundled zero-dependency LZ codec is supported
  threshold: 1024           // Min size to compress (bytes)
}
```

### Sync Configuration

```typescript
sync: {
  enabled: true,                // Enable cross-tab sync
  storages: ['localStorage'],   // Storages to sync (cross-tab fallback is localStorage-only)
  interval: 5000,               // Optional periodic sync interval (ms)
  conflictResolution: 'latest'  // 'latest' | 'merge' | custom function
}
```

> Cross-tab sync uses `BroadcastChannel` when available and falls back to
> `storage` events. Browsers only fire cross-tab `storage` events for
> `localStorage`; `sessionStorage` is tab-scoped and never propagates cross-tab.

### TTL Configuration

```typescript
ttl: {
  defaultTTL: 3600000,      // Default TTL in ms (1 hour)
  cleanupInterval: 60000,   // Cleanup sweep interval (ms)
  autoCleanup: true,        // Auto-remove expired items
  batchSize: 100,           // Max items removed per cleanup cycle
  slidingTTL: false,        // Reset TTL on access (instance default)
  onExpire: (keys) => {}    // Callback invoked with expired keys
}
```

## Environment-Specific Configuration

### Development

```typescript
const devConfig = {
  encryption: { enabled: false }, // Disable for debugging
  compression: { enabled: false },
  sync: {
    enabled: true,
    interval: 0 // 0 = event-driven (no polling)
  }
};
```

### Production

```typescript
const prodConfig = {
  encryption: { 
    enabled: true,
    password: process.env.STORAGE_KEY 
  },
  compression: { 
    enabled: true,
    threshold: 512 // Aggressive compression
  },
  ttl: {
    autoCleanup: true,
    cleanupInterval: 300000 // 5 minutes
  }
};
```

## Storage Selection

Strata does not use named "strategies." Instead, list the storage backends you
want in `defaultStorages`, in order of preference — Strata uses the first one
available on the current platform:

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  // Try persistent stores first, fall back to memory as a last resort
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory']
});
```

:::danger `defaultStorages` is not a registration list
It is the preference order for choosing the **default** adapter, and the fallback order when one is
unusable. `keys()`, `clear()` and `size()` with no explicit `storage` span every registered adapter;
`subscribe()` listens to registered adapters that support change events. Listing one storage here does not
stop the others from being registered or swept.

To leave an adapter out entirely, say so:

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['localStorage'],
  adapters: { sessionStorage: false, indexedDB: false, cookies: false, cache: false },
});
```

Since 2.9.0, `adapters: { <name>: false }` skips **registration**, not just initialization. (Before 2.9.0
it only skipped initialization, so the adapter was still registered and still swept — which is what made
`defaultStorages` look like a registration list that was being ignored.)
:::

## Key prefix and the 3.0.0 migration {#key-prefix}

Since **3.0.0**, `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` keys are written under **`strata:`**
(`DEFAULT_WEB_KEY_PREFIX`, exported). Existing data migrates itself on read.

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage();                              // keys at `strata:<key>`
const legacy  = defineStorage({ keyPrefix: false });          // pre-3.0, bare keys
const custom  = defineStorage({ keyPrefix: 'myapp:' });       // your own
const noMove  = defineStorage({ migrateLegacyKeys: false });  // don't adopt 2.x entries
```

:::danger Take `keyPrefix: false` when something outside this library reads a physical key
A pre-paint theme script that runs before any module loads, or a logger reading its own level, knows the
exact key name — and a prefix changes it underneath them. Migration keeps the *data* reachable through
this library; it cannot fix a hard-coded reader.
:::

**How migration works.** A miss at `strata:<key>` falls back to the bare `<key>`; if the value is one of
ours it is moved under the prefix and returned. It is **per key, on read** — never a bulk sweep, which
would adopt every unprefixed envelope on the origin including keys belonging to an instance that opted out
or a sibling app still on 2.x. It **never adopts a non-envelope**, and it **never overwrites** a value
already at the prefixed key. `keys()` lists not-yet-migrated entries so enumeration stays complete, but
listing never moves anything.

Unchanged: `cookies` (already `strata_`), `indexedDB` and `cache` (named stores), `memory` (its own Map),
`url` (already prefixes its params). `namespace` is a separate mechanism — the physical key is
`<keyPrefix><namespace>:<key>`.

## Shared storage areas and key ownership {#key-ownership}

`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and cookies are shared with every other script on the origin, and the
`localStorage` and `sessionStorage` use the `strata:` prefix by default since 3.0.0. **Since 2.9.0 an adapter identifies its own data by shape**
— a key is its own only when the stored value is a `StorageValue` envelope — so `keys()`, the TTL sweep
and `clear()` never touch data this library did not write.

Consequences worth knowing:

- A key written to the same area by anything else is invisible to `keys()` **by design**.
- A value we cannot read is skipped and reported at `debug`, not as an error: it is evidence the key
  belongs to somebody else, which is the ordinary case in a shared area.
- `setLogLevel('debug')` (exported) names every skipped key and why.

Setting `namespace` or a per-adapter `prefix` is still worth doing for a clean keyspace. It is no longer
what keeps this library off other applications' keys.


## Custom Configuration Patterns

### Multi-Instance Configuration

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

// User data storage
const userStorage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['secure', 'preferences']
});

// Cache storage
const cacheStorage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['cache', 'indexedDB'],
  ttl: { defaultTTL: 300000 } // 5 minutes
});

// Temporary storage
const tempStorage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['memory', 'sessionStorage'],
  ttl: { defaultTTL: 60000 } // 1 minute
});

// In a Capacitor app, before using userStorage on a device:
await registerCapacitorAdapters(userStorage);
```

If you also enable encryption, supply a password from a secure runtime source.

### Optional Features

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  compression: {
    enabled: true,
    threshold: 1024
  },
  sync: {
    enabled: typeof BroadcastChannel !== 'undefined'
  }
});
```

Encryption needs a password from a secure runtime source when you enable it; see the [encryption guide](./guides/features/encryption.md).

## Validation

Initialisation selects the first available registered adapter from `defaultStorages`. Encryption can be enabled without an instance password when each encrypted operation supplies `encryptionPassword`:

```typescript
try {
  const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } });
  await storage.initialize();
  await storage.set('private-draft', draft, {
    encryptionPassword: password,
  });
} catch (error) {
  // Show a setup or write failure in the application UI.
}
```

## Next Steps

- Explore [Storage Adapters](./api/adapters/README.md)
- Learn about [Encryption](./guides/features/encryption.md)
- Read about [Caching Patterns](./guides/patterns/caching.md)

# Advanced Encryption Examples
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/examples/advanced/encryption
================================================================================

# Advanced Encryption Examples

Strata's encryption manager runs only when the instance has `encryption.enabled: true`. `encrypt: true` on an instance without that configuration does not turn encryption on. These examples use the async API and a password supplied by the calling application.

## Basic Encryption

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } });
const password = await askUserForPassword();

await storage.set('private-draft', { text: 'First draft' }, {
  encryptionPassword: password,
});
const draft = await storage.get<{ text: string }>('private-draft', {
  encryptionPassword: password,
});
```

Do not put a real password in source code or persist it beside the ciphertext.

## Configuration Options

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  encryption: {
    enabled: true,
    algorithm: 'AES-GCM',
    keyLength: 256,
    iterations: 600_000,
    saltLength: 16,
  },
});
```

The package generates a fresh salt and IV for each encrypted write. `keySize` and a literal `salt` are not configuration options. Keep the same user password for later reads; each record carries the salt and iteration count needed for decryption.

## Platform-Specific Encryption

Web Crypto encryption works through the configured Strata instance. A Capacitor app can instead use the native `secure` adapter after registration:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage();
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
await storage.set('session_token', token, { storage: 'secure' });
```

Native behavior needs iOS and Android device verification. This API does not expose a biometric prompt or a per-call Keychain accessibility setting.

## Selective Encryption

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } });

await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { encrypt: false });
await storage.set('private-draft', draft, {
  encrypt: true,
  encryptionPassword: password,
});
```

A configured instance defaults to encryption for each write, so an intentionally plain value needs `encrypt: false`.

## Key Management

A password must be supplied again to read an encrypted value. If the application loses it, Strata cannot decrypt that value. Let the account or user flow own password recovery; the package does not provide an escrow service.

```typescript
try {
  const draft = await storage.get('private-draft', {
    encryptionPassword: password,
  });
  // Use draft only after the read succeeds.
} catch {
  // Show a local recovery path without logging the password or value.
}
```

## Real-World Examples

For a private draft, choose a storage backend with enough space and a useful expiry:

```typescript
await storage.set('draft:123', draft, {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
  encrypt: true,
  encryptionPassword: password,
  ttl: 86_400_000,
});
```

Do not store a card number or a server authentication secret merely because a local encryption option exists. Keep those flows with the service that owns them.

## Best Practices

- Enable encryption on the instance before the first encrypted write.
- Use the async API; synchronous reads and writes cannot encrypt or decrypt.
- Supply and protect the password outside the package.
- Verify a write-read round-trip on every intended platform.
- Use the native `secure` adapter for device-held credentials only after testing its native path.

## See Also

- [Encryption guide](../../guides/features/encryption.md)
- [Encryption API](../../api/features/encryption.md)
- [Basic encryption examples](../encryption.md)

# Queue consented analytics events
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/examples/analytics
================================================================================

# Queue consented analytics events

Strata Storage is a local key/value layer, not an analytics provider. You can use it to hold a small event outbox until your own endpoint accepts the events. Collect only after the user has given the consent your product requires, and keep sensitive values out of event properties.

- [Record an event](#record)
- [Replay the outbox](#replay)
- [Query and clear local records](#query)

<a id="record"></a>
## 📝 Record an event&nbsp;[#](#record)

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'analytics-example' });

type PageEvent = {
  id: string;
  name: 'page_view';
  path: string;
  occurredAt: number;
};

async function trackPageView(hasConsent: boolean): Promise<void> {
  if (!hasConsent) return;

  const event: PageEvent = {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    name: 'page_view',
    path: window.location.pathname,
    occurredAt: Date.now(),
  };
  await storage.set(`event:${event.id}`, event, {
    storage: 'indexedDB',
    ttl: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
  });
}
```

The event stores a path, not the full URL with query parameters. The 7-day TTL bounds the local queue; an event that expires before delivery is lost. Choose retention from your product's privacy policy and operational needs.

<a id="replay"></a>
## 📤 Replay the outbox&nbsp;[#](#replay)

```typescript
async function sendPendingEvents(): Promise<void> {
  const keys = await storage.keys(/^event:/, { storage: 'indexedDB' });

  for (const key of keys) {
    const event = await storage.get<PageEvent>(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
    if (!event) continue;

    try {
      const response = await fetch('/api/analytics', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          'Idempotency-Key': event.id,
        },
        body: JSON.stringify(event),
      });
      if (response.ok) await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
    } catch {
      // Keep the event for a later attempt.
    }
  }
}
```

`/api/analytics` is your own endpoint. It must validate the event, enforce consent and deduplicate the operation ID before accepting it. A failed HTTP status leaves the event queued. Aggregate counts and charts on the server; a client-side scan of local events cannot represent all users.

<a id="query"></a>
## 🔎 Query and clear local records&nbsp;[#](#query)

```typescript
const docsViews = await storage.query<PageEvent>({
  name: 'page_view',
  path: '/docs',
}, { storage: 'indexedDB' });

// When consent is withdrawn, stop tracking and clear this local outbox.
await storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB', prefix: 'event:' });
```

`query()` matches `name` and `path` because both fields are in the stored value. The result is this browser's local records only. If your app sends events to other providers too, consent withdrawal must cover those paths as well.


================================================================================
# Angular storage service
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/examples/angular-services
================================================================================

# Angular storage service

An Angular service can own one Strata instance and expose the operations your components need. This example keeps small drafts in browser `localStorage`, whose adapter emits change events. It doesn't implement authentication or a shared server database.

- [Draft service](#service)
- [Subscriptions and limits](#subscriptions)

<a id="service"></a>
## 🧩 Draft service&nbsp;[#](#service)

```typescript
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { defineStorage, type StorageChange } from 'strata-storage';

type Draft = {
  title: string;
  status: 'open' | 'closed';
};

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class DraftStorageService {
  private readonly storage = defineStorage({
    namespace: 'angular-drafts',
    defaultStorages: ['localStorage'],
  });

  async save(id: string, draft: Draft): Promise<void> {
    await this.storage.set(`draft:${id}`, draft, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  }

  async load(id: string): Promise<Draft | null> {
    return this.storage.get<Draft>(`draft:${id}`, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  }

  async remove(id: string): Promise<void> {
    await this.storage.remove(`draft:${id}`, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  }

  async listOpen(): Promise<Array<{ key: string; value: Draft }>> {
    return this.storage.query<Draft>({ status: 'open' }, {
      storage: 'localStorage',
    });
  }

  subscribe(onChange: (change: StorageChange) => void): () => void {
    return this.storage.subscribe(change => {
      if (change.key.startsWith('draft:')) onChange(change);
    }, { storage: 'localStorage' });
  }
}
```

Inject `DraftStorageService` into a component, call its async methods and show a pending or failure state around writes. `load()` returns `null` for a missing draft. The service uses only public methods; it never reaches into a private `.storage` field from another class.

<a id="subscriptions"></a>
## 🔄 Subscriptions and limits&nbsp;[#](#subscriptions)

`subscribe()` returns an unsubscribe function. A component that registers a callback should call it when the component is destroyed. The `localStorage` adapter emits local writes and browser storage events from other tabs. The `indexedDB` adapter does not advertise change observation, so don't move this subscription to IndexedDB and assume it will fire.

`query()` scans decoded local values. Keep the namespace dedicated to drafts, or add a value field to distinguish records. For large datasets, let your server query and aggregate the records.


================================================================================
# Basic CRUD Operations
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/examples/basic/crud
================================================================================

# Basic CRUD Operations

Learn how to perform Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations with Strata Storage.

## Table of Contents

- [Setup](#setup)
- [Create (Set)](#create-set)
- [Read (Get)](#read-get)
- [Update](#update)
- [Delete (Remove)](#delete-remove)
- [List Operations](#list-operations)
- [Multiple Items](#multiple-items)
- [Error Handling](#error-handling)

## Setup

First, create a web-ready instance. It initializes on the first operation:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
```

## Create (Set)

### Store Simple Values

```typescript
// String
await storage.set('username', 'john_doe');

// Number
await storage.set('age', 25);

// Boolean
await storage.set('isActive', true);

// Null
await storage.set('optionalValue', null);
```

### Store Objects

```typescript
await storage.set('user', {
  id: 123,
  name: 'John Doe',
  email: 'john@example.com',
  age: 25
});
```

### Store Arrays

```typescript
await storage.set('favoriteColors', ['red', 'blue', 'green']);

await storage.set('users', [
  { id: 1, name: 'John' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Jane' }
]);
```

### Store with Options

```typescript
// Specify storage adapter
await storage.set('largeData', bigObject, {
  storage: 'indexedDB'
});

// With TTL (expires in 1 hour)
await storage.set('sessionData', data, {
  ttl: 60 * 60 * 1000
});

// Enable encryption on a separate instance before asking it to encrypt.
const encryptedStorage = defineStorage({ encryption: { enabled: true } });
await encryptedStorage.set('sensitiveData', secret, {
  encryptionPassword: password
});

// Compression also needs instance configuration.
const compressedStorage = defineStorage({ compression: { enabled: true } });
await compressedStorage.set('hugeData', massiveObject);

// With tags for querying
await storage.set('document', content, {
  tags: ['work', 'important', '2024']
});
```

## Read (Get)

### Retrieve Simple Values

```typescript
const username = await storage.get('username');
console.log(username); // 'john_doe'

const age = await storage.get('age');
console.log(age); // 25

const isActive = await storage.get('isActive');
console.log(isActive); // true
```

### Retrieve Objects

```typescript
const user = await storage.get('user');
console.log(user);
// { id: 123, name: 'John Doe', email: 'john@example.com', age: 25 }

// Access properties
console.log(user.name); // 'John Doe'
console.log(user.email); // 'john@example.com'
```

### Retrieve Arrays

```typescript
const colors = await storage.get('favoriteColors');
console.log(colors); // ['red', 'blue', 'green']

const users = await storage.get('users');
console.log(users);
// [{ id: 1, name: 'John' }, { id: 2, name: 'Jane' }]
```

### Get with Default Value

```typescript
// If key doesn't exist, returns null
const theme = await storage.get('theme');
console.log(theme); // null

// Use || for default value
const themeWithDefault = await storage.get('theme') || 'light';
console.log(themeWithDefault); // 'light'

// Use ?? for null coalescing
const language = await storage.get('language') ?? 'en';
console.log(language); // 'en'
```

### Type-Safe Retrieval (TypeScript)

```typescript
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
}

const user = await storage.get<User>('user');

if (user) {
  // TypeScript knows user is User
  console.log(user.name); // Type-safe
}
```

### Get from Specific Adapter

```typescript
// Get from specific storage
const data = await storage.get('key', { storage: 'indexedDB' });
```

## Update

### Update Entire Value

```typescript
// Original
await storage.set('user', { id: 1, name: 'John', age: 25 });

// Update (replaces entire object)
await storage.set('user', { id: 1, name: 'John Doe', age: 26 });
```

### Update Object Property

```typescript
// Get current value
const user = await storage.get('user');

// Modify
user.age = 27;
user.email = 'newemail@example.com';

// Save back
await storage.set('user', user);
```

### Update with Spread Operator

```typescript
const user = await storage.get('user');

// Update specific properties
await storage.set('user', {
  ...user,
  age: 28,
  lastUpdated: new Date()
});
```

### Update Array

```typescript
// Add item to array
const colors = await storage.get('favoriteColors') || [];
colors.push('yellow');
await storage.set('favoriteColors', colors);

// Remove item from array
const users = await storage.get('users') || [];
const filteredUsers = users.filter(u => u.id !== 2);
await storage.set('users', filteredUsers);

// Update array item
const items = await storage.get('items') || [];
const updatedItems = items.map(item =>
  item.id === 3 ? { ...item, status: 'completed' } : item
);
await storage.set('items', updatedItems);
```

### Increment/Decrement

```typescript
// Increment counter
const count = await storage.get('counter') || 0;
await storage.set('counter', count + 1);

// Decrement
const score = await storage.get('score') || 100;
await storage.set('score', score - 10);
```

## Delete (Remove)

### Remove Single Item

```typescript
await storage.remove('username');

// Verify deletion
const username = await storage.get('username');
console.log(username); // null
```

### Remove Multiple Items

```typescript
await storage.remove('username');
await storage.remove('age');
await storage.remove('isActive');

// For a list of keys, wait for every removal
await Promise.all(['username', 'age', 'isActive'].map((key) => storage.remove(key)));
```

### Clear All Data

```typescript
// Remove everything
await storage.clear();

// Verify
const keys = await storage.keys();
console.log(keys); // []
```

### Clear Specific Adapter

```typescript
// Clear only localStorage
await storage.clear({ storage: 'localStorage' });

// Clear only indexedDB
await storage.clear({ storage: 'indexedDB' });
```

### Conditional Removal

```typescript
// Remove items matching condition
const allKeys = await storage.keys();

for (const key of allKeys) {
  if (key.startsWith('temp_')) {
    await storage.remove(key);
  }
}
```

## List Operations

### Get All Keys

```typescript
const keys = await storage.keys();
console.log(keys); // ['username', 'user', 'settings', ...]
```

### Get All Data

```typescript
const keys = await storage.keys();
const allData = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(
  keys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)])
));
console.log(allData);
// {
//   username: 'john_doe',
//   user: { id: 123, name: 'John' },
//   settings: { theme: 'dark' }
// }
```

### Check if Key Exists

```typescript
const hasUsername = await storage.has('username');
console.log(hasUsername); // true

const hasUnknown = await storage.has('nonexistent');
console.log(hasUnknown); // false
```

### Get Storage Size

```typescript
const size = await storage.size();
console.log(`Storage contains ${size.count} items`);
console.log(`Storage uses approximately ${size.total} bytes`);
```

## Multiple Items

These calls run independently. If one fails, earlier writes may already have succeeded.

### Set Multiple Items

```typescript
await Promise.all([
  storage.set('username', 'john_doe'),
  storage.set('email', 'john@example.com'),
  storage.set('age', 25)
]);
```

### Get Multiple Items

```typescript
const keys = ['username', 'email', 'age'];
const values = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(
  keys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)])
));
console.log(values);
// {
//   username: 'john_doe',
//   email: 'john@example.com',
//   age: 25
// }
```

### Remove Multiple Items

```typescript
await Promise.all(['username', 'email', 'age'].map((key) => storage.remove(key)));
```

### Per-Item Options

```typescript
await storage.set('user1', data1, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
await storage.set('user2', data2, { encrypt: true, encryptionPassword: password });
await storage.set('user3', data3, { ttl: 3600000 });
```

## Error Handling

### Try-Catch Pattern

```typescript
try {
  await storage.set('key', 'value');
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Failed to set value:', error);
}
```

### Handle Specific Errors

```typescript
import {
  StorageError,
  QuotaExceededError,
  StorageNotAvailableError
} from 'strata-storage';

try {
  await storage.set('largeData', hugeObject);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof QuotaExceededError) {
    console.error('Storage quota exceeded');
    // Clear old data or use different adapter
    await storage.clear();
  } else if (error instanceof StorageNotAvailableError) {
    console.error('Storage not available');
    // Use fallback
    await storage.set('largeData', hugeObject, { storage: 'memory' });
  } else if (error instanceof StorageError) {
    console.error('Storage error:', error.message);
  }
}
```

### Safe Operations

```typescript
// Safely get with default
async function safeGet(key: string, defaultValue: any) {
  try {
    const value = await storage.get(key);
    return value ?? defaultValue;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`Failed to get ${key}:`, error);
    return defaultValue;
  }
}

// Safely set
async function safeSet(key: string, value: any) {
  try {
    await storage.set(key, value);
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`Failed to set ${key}:`, error);
    return false;
  }
}

// Usage
const theme = await safeGet('theme', 'light');
const success = await safeSet('theme', 'dark');
```

## Complete Example

Here's a complete example demonstrating all CRUD operations:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

async function crudExample() {
  // Setup
  const storage = defineStorage();

  // CREATE
  await storage.set('user', {
    id: 1,
    name: 'John Doe',
    email: 'john@example.com',
    preferences: {
      theme: 'dark',
      language: 'en'
    }
  });

  console.log('User created');

  // READ
  const user = await storage.get('user');
  console.log('User data:', user);

  // UPDATE
  const updatedUser = {
    ...user,
    name: 'John Smith',
    preferences: {
      ...user.preferences,
      theme: 'light'
    }
  };
  await storage.set('user', updatedUser);
  console.log('User updated');

  // READ AGAIN
  const currentUser = await storage.get('user');
  console.log('Updated user:', currentUser);

  // LIST
  const allKeys = await storage.keys();
  console.log('All keys:', allKeys);

  const allData = Object.fromEntries(await Promise.all(
    allKeys.map(async (key) => [key, await storage.get(key)])
  ));
  console.log('All data:', allData);

  // DELETE
  await storage.remove('user');
  console.log('User deleted');

  // VERIFY
  const deletedUser = await storage.get('user');
  console.log('User after deletion:', deletedUser); // null
}

// Run the example
crudExample();
```

- See [Real-World Examples](../README.md)
- Explore [Storage Adapters](../../api/adapters/README.md)

# Basic Usage Examples
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/examples/basic-usage
================================================================================

# Basic Usage Examples

Simple examples to get started with Strata Storage.

## Installation

```bash
npm install strata-storage
# or
yarn add strata-storage
```

## Basic Operations

### Store and Retrieve Data

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();

// Store data
await storage.set('user_name', 'John Doe');
await storage.set('user_age', 30);
await storage.set('user_preferences', {
  theme: 'dark',
  language: 'en',
  notifications: true
});

// Retrieve data
const name = await storage.get('user_name');
console.log(name); // 'John Doe'

const preferences = await storage.get('user_preferences');
console.log(preferences); // { theme: 'dark', ... }
```

### Remove Data

```typescript
// Remove single item
await storage.remove('user_age');

// Clear all data
await storage.clear();
```

### Check Existence

```typescript
// Check if key exists
const exists = await storage.has('user_name');
console.log(exists); // true or false

// Get all keys
const keys = await storage.keys();
console.log(keys); // ['user_name', 'user_preferences', ...]
```

## Storage Options

### Specify Storage Type

```typescript
// Use specific storage
await storage.set('session_data', data, {
  storage: 'sessionStorage'
});

await storage.set('persistent_data', data, {
  storage: 'localStorage'
});

await storage.set('large_data', data, {
  storage: 'indexedDB'
});
```

### Set Expiration

```typescript
// Data expires in 1 hour
await storage.set('temp_token', token, {
  ttl: 3600000 // milliseconds
});

// Data expires at specific time
await storage.set('daily_cache', data, {
  expireAt: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
});
```

## Working with Complex Data

### Objects and Arrays

```typescript
// Store complex objects
const user = {
  id: 123,
  name: 'John Doe',
  email: 'john@example.com',
  roles: ['user', 'admin'],
  metadata: {
    lastLogin: new Date(),
    loginCount: 42
  }
};

await storage.set('current_user', user);

// Retrieve and use
const savedUser = await storage.get('current_user');
console.log(savedUser.roles); // ['user', 'admin']
```

### Binary Data

```typescript
// Store ArrayBuffer
const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(256);
await storage.set('binary_data', buffer);

// Store Blob
const blob = new Blob(['Hello World'], { type: 'text/plain' });
await storage.set('file_blob', blob);

// Store Uint8Array
const bytes = new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
await storage.set('byte_array', bytes);
```

## Error Handling

```typescript
try {
  await storage.set('key', 'value');
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED') {
    console.error('Storage quota exceeded');
  } else {
    console.error('Storage error:', error);
  }
}

// Safe get with default value
const value = await storage.get('maybe_missing') || 'default';
```

## Batch Operations

```typescript
// Set multiple values
const items = {
  'user:1': { name: 'Alice' },
  'user:2': { name: 'Bob' },
  'user:3': { name: 'Charlie' }
};

for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(items)) {
  await storage.set(key, value);
}

// Get multiple values
const userIds = ['user:1', 'user:2', 'user:3'];
const users = [];

for (const id of userIds) {
  const user = await storage.get(id);
  if (user) users.push(user);
}
```

## Namespace Support

```typescript
// Create namespaced storage
const userStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'users' });
const appStorage = defineStorage({ namespace: 'app' });

// Data is isolated
await userStorage.set('data', 'user data');
await appStorage.set('data', 'app data');

const userData = await userStorage.get('data'); // 'user data'
const appData = await appStorage.get('data'); // 'app data'
```

## Platform Detection

```typescript
// Browser storage; native adapters need explicit registration
const storage = defineStorage();

// On web: prefers localStorage, then IndexedDB, sessionStorage and memory.
// On iOS/Android: register native adapters before selecting them.
// See the Capacitor platform guide for device setup.

await storage.set('cross_platform', 'Works everywhere!');
```

## Next Steps

- [Configuration Options](./configuration.md)
- [Error Handling](./error-handling.md)
- [Advanced Features](../configuration.md)
