# Cross-tab sync
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/features/sync
================================================================================

# Cross-Tab Sync Guide

Strata Storage can notify another browser tab when a value changes. `BroadcastChannel` is the primary path. The browser's `storage` event is a `localStorage` fallback; `sessionStorage` does not cross tabs through that event.

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['localStorage', 'memory'],
  sync: { enabled: true, storages: ['localStorage'] },
});

const unsubscribe = storage.subscribe((change) => {
  if (change.source === 'remote' && change.key === 'draft') {
    // Reload this key into your own UI state.
  }
});

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' }, {
  storage: 'localStorage',
});

// When the screen or app shell is removed:
unsubscribe();
```

The receiving tab should read the key again when it gets a remote notification. A notification is not an atomic merge of two simultaneous writes.

## Configuration

```typescript
const storage = defineStorage({
  sync: {
    enabled: true,
    storages: ['localStorage', 'indexedDB'],
    conflictResolution: 'latest',
  },
});
```

`sync` accepts `enabled`, `storages`, `interval` and `conflictResolution` (`'latest'`, `'merge'`, or a callback). There is no per-call `syncEnabled` option or top-level `onLog` hook. If a key must stay local, put it in a storage type outside the configured sync list or use a separate instance.

## Limits

- `sessionStorage` is tab scoped; do not use it as a cross-tab fallback.
- A storage event on `localStorage` is raised by writes in another tab, not the current one.
- Native iOS and Android storage behavior needs device verification; this browser guide does not prove cross-device sync.

## See Also

- [Sync API reference](../../api/features/sync.md)
- [Web platform guide](../platforms/web.md)


================================================================================
# Time-to-live guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/features/ttl
================================================================================

# Time-to-Live (TTL) Guide

`ttl` is a duration in milliseconds. `expireAt` is a `Date` or an absolute epoch-millisecond timestamp. A read of an expired key returns `null`.

## Quick Start

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  ttl: { autoCleanup: true, cleanupInterval: 60_000 },
});

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' }, {
  ttl: 3_600_000,
});
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');
```

`defineStorage()` registers the web adapters and initializes on first use. Call `registerCapacitorAdapters(storage)` before selecting a native adapter in a Capacitor app.

## Expiration Options

```typescript
await storage.set('short_cache', data, { ttl: 300_000 });
await storage.set('daily_cache', data, {
  expireAt: new Date('2027-01-01T00:00:00Z'),
});
await storage.set('active_session', data, {
  ttl: 1_800_000,
  sliding: true,
});
```

`sliding: true` extends an item's expiry on access. `expireAfter` is a backward-compatible alias of **absolute** `expireAt`; for a duration from now, use `ttl`.

## Inspect and Change Expiry

```typescript
const remainingMs = await storage.getTTL('short_cache');
await storage.extendTTL('short_cache', 60_000);
const expiring = await storage.getExpiring(300_000);
await storage.persist('short_cache');
const removed = await storage.cleanupExpired();
```

`getTTL()` returns `null` for a key without an expiry. `extendTTL()` requires an existing key. `persist()` removes its expiry. `getExpiring()` returns keys and `expiresIn` values inside the requested window. `cleanupExpired()` returns the number removed. There is no `setTTL()` method on the public `Strata` instance; write the value again with a new `ttl` or `expireAt` when that is what you need.

## Cleanup Configuration

`StrataConfig.ttl` accepts `defaultTTL`, `cleanupInterval`, `autoCleanup`, `batchSize`, `slidingTTL` and `onExpire`. The default cleanup interval is 60 seconds; `autoCleanup: false` disables the periodic sweep. A value can still be treated as expired when read.

## See Also

- [TTL API reference](../../api/features/ttl.md)
- [Caching patterns](../patterns/caching.md)


================================================================================
# Caching patterns
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/patterns/caching
================================================================================

# Caching Patterns with Strata Storage

A cache entry should have a key, a freshness limit, and a way to invalidate it when the source changes. Strata Storage supplies key-value operations and TTL; your application decides when it is safe to use a cached value.

## Cache-Aside Pattern

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const cache = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});

async function getCached<T>(
  key: string,
  fetchFresh: () => Promise<T>,
  ttl: number,
): Promise<T> {
  const cached = await cache.get<T>(key);
  if (cached !== null) return cached;

  const value = await fetchFresh();
  await cache.set(key, value, { ttl });
  return value;
}
```

`defineStorage()` registers the web adapters. The first available `defaultStorages` entry becomes the default. An expired key reads as `null`; the next request calls `fetchFresh`.

## Invalidation

```typescript
await cache.remove('product:123');

const keys = await cache.keys(/^product:/);
for (const key of keys) {
  await cache.remove(key);
}
```

If a single Strata instance has several registered adapters, pass `{ storage: 'indexedDB' }` to each call when you need to target exactly that backend. A key's namespace and physical prefix are separate from a cache invalidation pattern.

## Cache API Adapter

The Strata `cache` adapter uses browser Cache storage for **string-keyed, JSON-serializable values**. It does not round-trip native `Request` or `Response` objects. Use the browser Cache API directly for HTTP request/response matching, or keep the response body as a serializable value in Strata.

```typescript
await cache.set('api:/items', { items: ['one', 'two'] }, {
  storage: 'cache',
  ttl: 300_000,
});
```

The adapter is available in a supported browser page with `window.caches`; the current implementation does not run in a service worker global scope.

## Platform Limits

The package is client-side key-value storage. It does not provide a shared server cache or a Node SQLite backend. In a Capacitor app, register native adapters before selecting `sqlite` or `preferences`; see the [Capacitor guide](../platforms/capacitor.md).

## See Also

- [TTL guide](../features/ttl.md)
- [Cache adapter](../../api/adapters/web/cache.md)


================================================================================
# Session state patterns
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/patterns/sessions
================================================================================

# Session State Patterns

Strata Storage can retain **client-side state** for a browser tab or across reloads. It does not create, validate, revoke, or synchronize a server authentication session. Keep authentication and authorization on the server; issue an `HttpOnly` cookie there if the application needs a browser session credential.

## Tab-Scoped State

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  namespace: 'checkout-draft',
  defaultStorages: ['sessionStorage', 'memory'],
});

await storage.set('step', 2, {
  storage: 'sessionStorage',
  ttl: 1_800_000,
});
const step = await storage.get<number>('step', {
  storage: 'sessionStorage',
});
```

`sessionStorage` survives a reload in the same tab but is tab scoped. If you want state that survives closing the tab, choose `localStorage` or `indexedDB` explicitly and account for the longer retention.

## Sign-Out Cleanup

```typescript
const keys = await storage.keys(/^draft:/, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
for (const key of keys) {
  await storage.remove(key, { storage: 'sessionStorage' });
}
```

Clear application state on sign-out after the server ends the authentication session. `clear({ storage: 'sessionStorage', prefix: 'draft:' })` is also available when the whole matching set belongs to this instance.

## Native State

A Capacitor app can select `secure` for a sensitive local value after calling `registerCapacitorAdapters(storage)`. The public `StorageOptions` has no biometric prompt or Keychain accessibility option; the [iOS](../platforms/ios.md) and [Android](../platforms/android.md) guides describe the supported boundary. Verify native persistence on device.

## See Also

- [TTL guide](../features/ttl.md)
- [Sync guide](../features/sync.md)


================================================================================
# Android platform guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/android
================================================================================

# Android Platform Guide

Strata Storage's Capacitor plugin provides `preferences` (SharedPreferences), `secure` (encrypted preferences), `sqlite` and `filesystem` adapters on Android.

## Installation

```bash
yarn add strata-storage
yarn cap sync android
```

The package's Android build declares SDK 36 defaults, a minimum SDK of 23, and `androidx.security:security-crypto:1.1.0`. The host app's Android project can override SDK versions; inspect its merged configuration before release.

## Native Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'],
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' });
await storage.set('draft:1', { title: 'First draft' }, { storage: 'sqlite' });
await storage.set('token', token, { storage: 'secure' });
```

Native adapters require a running Capacitor Android app. The Filesystem adapter uses the app's internal directory, so this API does not require broad external-storage permissions. Do not add `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` or legacy read/write permissions for these adapter operations.

## Storage Choices

| Adapter | Use for | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `preferences` | Small app settings | Not encrypted |
| `secure` | Sensitive key-value data | No biometric prompt option through `StorageOptions` |
| `sqlite` | Larger structured key-value sets | Top-level `Strata` has no atomic `transaction()` API |
| `filesystem` | One file-backed JSON value per key | No directory option per call |

The `adapters.preferences` and `adapters.secure` config fields are booleans. Per-call options such as `directory`, `allowBackup`, `keyAlias` and `userAuthenticationRequired` are not in the public TypeScript API. Handle Android backup policy in the host app's native configuration rather than a Strata `set()` option.

## Verification

Run the [native device matrix](./device-verification.md) after syncing the package. Check read/write, persistence after force-stop, SQLite isolation, and file-backed operations on a device or emulator. The native bridge is not exercised by a web browser.

## See Also

- [Capacitor guide](./capacitor.md)
- [SQLite adapter](../../api/adapters/capacitor/sqlite.md)
- [Secure adapter](../../api/adapters/capacitor/secure.md)


================================================================================
# Capacitor platform guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/capacitor
================================================================================

# Capacitor Platform Guide

Strata Storage ships web adapters in its main entry point. Native `preferences`, `sqlite`, `secure` and `filesystem` adapters are opt-in through `strata-storage/capacitor`.

## Installation

```bash
yarn add strata-storage @capacitor/core
yarn cap sync
```

Build and sync the host app's native projects after installing the package. The native plugin only runs inside a Capacitor iOS or Android app.

## Basic Setup

```typescript
import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: Capacitor.isNativePlatform()
    ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory']
    : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');
```

`defineStorage()` registers the web adapters. `registerCapacitorAdapters()` adds the native adapters and refreshes the instance on a native platform; it returns without registering them in a browser. Call it before the first native operation. Use a single prepared instance in your app rather than creating one for every screen.

## Platform Detection

```typescript
import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core';

const platform = Capacitor.getPlatform(); // 'web', 'ios' or 'android'
const native = Capacitor.isNativePlatform();
```

Choose an adapter explicitly when a value has a specific storage requirement:

```typescript
await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' });
await storage.set('session_token', token, { storage: 'secure', ttl: 3_600_000 });
```

The `storage` option selects a registered adapter. It does not make `preferences` available in the browser. Keep web fallbacks in your `defaultStorages` list for shared code, and test each explicit native path on a device.

## Native Adapter Configuration

`StrataConfig.adapters.preferences` and `.secure` accept booleans. The top-level `StorageOptions` does not expose biometric prompts, per-call filesystem directories, or Android preference file names. For separate SQLite databases, create distinct `SqliteAdapter` instances, register each with its own `Strata` instance, then call `refreshAdapters()`; see the [SQLite adapter reference](../../api/adapters/capacitor/sqlite.md).

## Testing

Use the [device verification guide](./device-verification.md) on both iOS and Android. A browser test exercises web adapters and the plugin's fallback, not native persistence. After changing native code, sync and rebuild the host app before testing.

## See Also

- [Android guide](./android.md)
- [iOS guide](./ios.md)
- [Web guide](./web.md)


================================================================================
# Device Verification Guide — Native Storage (v2.6.0)
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/device-verification
================================================================================

# Device Verification Guide — Native Storage (v2.6.0)

> **Audience:** The package author (or a contributor who has Xcode and Android Studio available).
>
> **Purpose:** The quality gates (typecheck + build + lint) cover the JS/TS layer but cannot reach the native bridge. Every change to the iOS Swift or Android Java code must be verified by hand on a simulator or real device. This guide gives you the exact steps and the expected results so nothing is skipped.
>
> **v2.6.0 scope:** SQLite multi-store isolation, value round-trip shape, `size(true)` response, the new Filesystem backend, and `androidx.security 1.1.0` on Android.

---

## Contents

1. [Why native verification cannot be automated](#1-why-native-verification-cannot-be-automated)
2. [Host app setup](#2-host-app-setup)
3. [Test matrix](#3-test-matrix)
   - [3.1 Preferences (UserDefaults / SharedPreferences)](#31-preferences-userdefaults--sharedpreferences)
   - [3.2 Secure (Keychain / EncryptedSharedPreferences)](#32-secure-keychain--encryptedsharedpreferences)
   - [3.3 SQLite](#33-sqlite)
   - [3.4 Filesystem (new in v2.6.0)](#34-filesystem-new-in-v260)
   - [3.5 `isAvailable` per storage type](#35-isavailable-per-storage-type)
4. [Expected-vs-actual checklist](#4-expected-vs-actual-checklist)
5. [Troubleshooting](#5-troubleshooting)

---

## 1. Why native verification cannot be automated

The Capacitor bridge serialises every call from JavaScript to a native method registered in `StrataStoragePlugin.m`. In any web/Node environment `isCapacitor()` returns `false` and every `StrataStorage.*` call goes to the web fallback — there is no way to boot an iOS or Android runtime outside a real device or simulator.

This means four things cannot be verified outside a real device:

- **SQLite multi-store** — whether two `SqliteAdapter` instances with different `database`/`table` values produce physically separate tables on disk.
- **Value round-trip shape** — whether native `get` returns the full `StorageValue` wrapper (with `created`, `updated`, `expires`, `tags`, `metadata`) rather than just the inner value.
- **`size(true)`** — whether the native side populates the `detailed.keys / values / metadata` byte breakdown.
- **Filesystem** — whether reads and writes actually land in the app's documents directory on both platforms.

The CAP_PLUGIN macro in `StrataStoragePlugin.m` is the registration point: if a method is missing from that list, every JS call to it silently returns `undefined`. Check that list first whenever a method appears unavailable.

---

## 2. Host app setup

You need a Capacitor app that lists `strata-storage` as a local dependency. The demo app at `example-apps/demo-app/` is the canonical choice. If you prefer a clean scratch app, the steps below create one from nothing.

### 2.1 Create (or reuse) a Capacitor host app

```bash
# Option A — use the existing demo app
cd /path/to/strata-storage/example-apps/demo-app
yarn install

# Option B — create a minimal host from scratch
mkdir strata-verify && cd strata-verify
yarn init -y
yarn add @capacitor/core @capacitor/cli @capacitor/ios @capacitor/android
npx cap init StrataVerify com.example.strataverify --web-dir dist
```

### 2.2 Point to your local build of strata-storage

Build the package first, then use a `file:` reference so the host app sees your exact native source.

```bash
# From the strata-storage root
yarn build

# In your host app's package.json, add:
# "strata-storage": "file:../../"   (adjust the relative path)
yarn install
```

### 2.3 Add native platforms (skip if they already exist)

```bash
npx cap add ios
npx cap add android
```

### 2.4 Sync

Sync must be run every time you rebuild `strata-storage` or touch any native file.

```bash
npx cap sync ios
npx cap sync android
```

`cap sync` copies the built JS bundle and the native plugin into the Xcode and Gradle projects. It does not install CocoaPods.

### 2.5 iOS — CocoaPods / SPM

```bash
cd ios/App
pod install
cd ../..
```

If the project uses Swift Package Manager instead of CocoaPods, open `ios/App/App.xcworkspace` in Xcode, navigate to **File > Packages > Resolve Package Versions**, and wait for resolution to finish.

Open the workspace — never the `.xcodeproj` directly:

```bash
npx cap open ios
# or: open ios/App/App.xcworkspace
```

Select a simulator or connected device in the Xcode toolbar, then press **Run** (⌘R).

### 2.6 Android — Gradle sync

```bash
npx cap open android
```

Android Studio opens. Wait for **Gradle sync** to complete (progress bar at the bottom). If sync fails, check **Build > Sync Project with Gradle Files** and review the **Build** output pane for errors.

Select an emulator or connected device in the device dropdown, then press **Run** (the green triangle).

### 2.7 Plumbing the test script into the app

The simplest approach is to add a button in the host app that calls a `runStorageTests()` function and prints results to a visible `<pre>` element or to the native log. The snippets in §3 are self-contained async functions you can call from that button. Use `console.log` (visible in Xcode's device console and in `adb logcat`) to capture pass/fail output while you work through the matrix.

---

## 3. Test matrix

All snippets use `defineStorage()` from `strata-storage`. Import it at the top of your test file:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { PreferencesAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';
import { SecureAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';
import { SqliteAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';
import { FilesystemAdapter } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';
```

Each section is independent. You can run them in any order and in isolation.

---

### 3.1 Preferences (UserDefaults / SharedPreferences)

**Native backing:** `NSUserDefaults` on iOS, `SharedPreferences` on Android. Data persists across app restarts but is not encrypted. Do not store tokens or credentials here.

```typescript
async function testPreferences() {
  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['preferences'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(new PreferencesAdapter());
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  // --- set / get round-trip ---
  await storage.set('pref_test_key', 'hello-native', { storage: 'preferences' });
  const got = await storage.get<string>('pref_test_key', { storage: 'preferences' });
  console.assert(got === 'hello-native', 'FAIL preferences: get after set');

  // --- keys ---
  await storage.set('pref_key_a', 1, { storage: 'preferences' });
  await storage.set('pref_key_b', 2, { storage: 'preferences' });
  const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'preferences' });
  console.assert(keys.includes('pref_test_key'), 'FAIL preferences: keys missing pref_test_key');
  console.assert(keys.includes('pref_key_a'), 'FAIL preferences: keys missing pref_key_a');

  // --- remove ---
  await storage.remove('pref_key_a', { storage: 'preferences' });
  const afterRemove = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'preferences' });
  console.assert(!afterRemove.includes('pref_key_a'), 'FAIL preferences: key still present after remove');

  // --- clear ---
  await storage.clear({ storage: 'preferences' });
  const afterClear = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'preferences' });
  console.assert(afterClear.length === 0, 'FAIL preferences: keys not empty after clear');

  console.log('PASS preferences');
}
```

**Expected results:**

| Step | Expected |
|------|----------|
| `get` after `set` | Returns `'hello-native'` (string, not null) |
| `keys` | Array includes both written keys |
| `keys` after `remove` | `pref_key_a` absent; other keys present |
| `keys` after `clear` | Empty array `[]` |

**Persistence check:** Stop the app completely (swipe away on iOS, force-stop on Android), relaunch it, and call `storage.get('pref_test_key', { storage: 'preferences' })` before calling `clear`. It must still return `'hello-native'`.

---

### 3.2 Secure (Keychain / EncryptedSharedPreferences)

**Native backing:** iOS Keychain (`SecItemAdd`/`SecItemCopyMatching`); Android `EncryptedSharedPreferences` backed by `androidx.security:security-crypto 1.1.0`. The encryption is managed entirely by the OS — no application-level key is required.

**Android note:** `androidx.security 1.1.0` (stable) is a hard requirement for v2.6.0. Open `android/app/build.gradle` and confirm `implementation "androidx.security:security-crypto:1.1.0"` (not an alpha tag). If Gradle sync fails after this change, run **File > Sync Project with Gradle Files** from Android Studio; the most common fix is bumping `compileSdkVersion` to 34.

```typescript
async function testSecure() {
  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['secure'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(new SecureAdapter());
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  const secret = 'super-secret-token-abc123';
  await storage.set('secure_token', secret, { storage: 'secure' });

  // --- basic round-trip ---
  const got = await storage.get<string>('secure_token', { storage: 'secure' });
  console.assert(got === secret, 'FAIL secure: get after set');

  // --- keys and remove ---
  const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'secure' });
  console.assert(keys.includes('secure_token'), 'FAIL secure: key missing from keys()');

  await storage.remove('secure_token', { storage: 'secure' });
  const gone = await storage.get<string>('secure_token', { storage: 'secure' });
  console.assert(gone === null, 'FAIL secure: key still readable after remove');

  console.log('PASS secure');
}
```

**Persistence across app restart:** This is the most important property of the Secure adapter. After calling `set`, force-quit the app and relaunch. Then:

```typescript
// Run this in isolation AFTER relaunching the app — do NOT call clear() before restarting
const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['secure'],
});
storage.registerAdapter(new SecureAdapter());
await storage.refreshAdapters();
const token = await storage.get<string>('secure_token', { storage: 'secure' });
console.assert(token === 'super-secret-token-abc123', 'FAIL secure: not persisted across restart');
console.log('PASS secure persistence');
```

**Expected results:**

| Step | Expected |
|------|----------|
| `get` after `set` | Returns the exact secret string |
| `keys` | Contains `'secure_token'` |
| `get` after `remove` | Returns `null` |
| `get` after app restart | Returns the exact secret string (Keychain / EncryptedSharedPreferences survived the restart) |

---

### 3.3 SQLite

SQLite receives the most changes in v2.6.0. There are four things to verify: (a) the full `StorageValue` wrapper survives a round-trip, (b) TTL expiry returns null after the deadline, (c) two adapter instances with different `database`/`table` do not share data, and (d) `size(true)` returns the `detailed` breakdown.

#### 3.3a Value round-trip with tags, TTL, and metadata

```typescript
async function testSqliteRoundTrip() {
  const sqlite = new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'strata', table: 'storage' });
  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['sqlite'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(sqlite);
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  const payload = {
    userId: 'u_001',
    profile: { name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' },
    scores: [10, 20, 30],
  };

  await storage.set('rt_test', payload, {
    storage: 'sqlite',
    tags: ['user', 'profile'],
    expireAt: Date.now() + 60_000,          // 60 s from now
    metadata: { source: 'verify-run' },
  });

  const wrapper = await sqlite.get<typeof payload>('rt_test');

  // Shape assertions — these all fail if native returns a bare value instead of the wrapper
  console.assert(wrapper !== null, 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: get returned null');
  console.assert(typeof wrapper?.created === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: created missing');
  console.assert(typeof wrapper?.updated === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: updated missing');
  console.assert(typeof wrapper?.expires === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: expires missing');
  console.assert(Array.isArray(wrapper?.tags), 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: tags not an array');
  console.assert(wrapper?.tags?.includes('profile'), 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: tag "profile" missing');
  console.assert(wrapper?.metadata?.source === 'verify-run', 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: metadata wrong');

  // Value shape
  console.assert(wrapper?.value?.userId === 'u_001', 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: value.userId wrong');
  console.assert(wrapper?.value?.scores?.length === 3, 'FAIL sqlite round-trip: value.scores length wrong');

  console.log('PASS sqlite round-trip');
}
```

**What is being verified:** Before v2.6.0 the native `get` handler returned the raw column bytes rather than the full `StorageValue<T>` object. The JS adapter does `result.value as StorageValue<T>` — if native sends back only the inner value, all the shape checks above fail.

#### 3.3b TTL expiry

```typescript
async function testSqliteTtl() {
  const sqlite = new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'strata', table: 'storage' });
  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['sqlite'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(sqlite);
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  // Write with a 1-second TTL
  await storage.set('ttl_test', 'ephemeral', {
    storage: 'sqlite',
    expireAt: Date.now() + 1_000,
  });

  // Immediately readable
  const before = await storage.get<string>('ttl_test', { storage: 'sqlite' });
  console.assert(before === 'ephemeral', 'FAIL sqlite TTL: not readable before expiry');

  // Wait for expiry
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1_500));

  const after = await storage.get<string>('ttl_test', { storage: 'sqlite' });
  console.assert(after === null, 'FAIL sqlite TTL: key still readable after expiry');

  console.log('PASS sqlite TTL');
}
```

#### 3.3c Multi-store isolation (new in v2.6.0)

This is the core of the multi-store contract: two `SqliteAdapter` instances with different `database` or `table` parameters must map to separate physical tables and never bleed data into each other.

```typescript
async function testSqliteMultiStore() {
  // Adapter A — database 'alpha', table 'main'
  const adapterA = new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'alpha', table: 'main' });
  const storageA = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['sqlite'],
  });
  storageA.registerAdapter(adapterA);
  await storageA.refreshAdapters();

  // Adapter B — database 'beta', table 'main'
  const adapterB = new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'beta', table: 'main' });
  const storageB = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['sqlite'],
  });
  storageB.registerAdapter(adapterB);
  await storageB.refreshAdapters();

  // Write the SAME key with different values to each store
  await storageA.set('collision_key', 'value-from-alpha', { storage: 'sqlite' });
  await storageB.set('collision_key', 'value-from-beta', { storage: 'sqlite' });

  const fromA = await storageA.get<string>('collision_key', { storage: 'sqlite' });
  const fromB = await storageB.get<string>('collision_key', { storage: 'sqlite' });

  console.assert(fromA === 'value-from-alpha', 'FAIL sqlite multi-store: alpha value wrong');
  console.assert(fromB === 'value-from-beta', 'FAIL sqlite multi-store: beta value wrong');
  console.assert(fromA !== fromB, 'FAIL sqlite multi-store: stores are not isolated');

  // Clearing one store must not affect the other
  await storageA.clear({ storage: 'sqlite' });
  const afterClearA = await storageA.get<string>('collision_key', { storage: 'sqlite' });
  const stillInB = await storageB.get<string>('collision_key', { storage: 'sqlite' });

  console.assert(afterClearA === null, 'FAIL sqlite multi-store: clear did not remove from alpha');
  console.assert(stillInB === 'value-from-beta', 'FAIL sqlite multi-store: clear leaked into beta');

  console.log('PASS sqlite multi-store');
}
```

**What is being verified:** Before v2.6.0 the `database` and `table` parameters were passed through the JS adapter but the native handler ignored them, mapping every adapter to the same `strata_storage.db / storage` table. Both stores would return whichever value was written last. After the fix, `alpha.db` and `beta.db` are distinct files on disk.

#### 3.3d `size(true)` shape

```typescript
async function testSqliteDetailedSize() {
  const sqlite = new SqliteAdapter({ database: 'strata', table: 'storage' });
  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['sqlite'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(sqlite);
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  // Seed a couple of entries so size is non-zero
  await storage.set('sz_a', { x: 1 }, { storage: 'sqlite', tags: ['t1'] });
  await storage.set('sz_b', 'plain string', { storage: 'sqlite' });

  const info = await sqlite.size(true);

  console.assert(typeof info.total === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite size: total not a number');
  console.assert(typeof info.count === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite size: count not a number');
  console.assert(info.count >= 2, 'FAIL sqlite size: count below 2 after seeding');

  // v2.6.0 contract — these must be populated when detailed=true
  console.assert(info.detailed !== undefined, 'FAIL sqlite size: detailed undefined');
  console.assert(typeof info.detailed?.keys === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite size: detailed.keys not a number');
  console.assert(typeof info.detailed?.values === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite size: detailed.values not a number');
  console.assert(typeof info.detailed?.metadata === 'number', 'FAIL sqlite size: detailed.metadata not a number');

  // Sanity: the sum of the three columns should be close to total
  const colSum = (info.detailed?.keys ?? 0) + (info.detailed?.values ?? 0) + (info.detailed?.metadata ?? 0);
  // Allow for padding / overhead — just check it's within an order of magnitude
  console.assert(colSum > 0 && colSum <= info.total * 5, 'FAIL sqlite size: column sum implausible');

  console.log('PASS sqlite size detailed', info);
}
```

**Expected `info` shape:**

```json
{
  "total": 312,
  "count": 2,
  "detailed": {
    "keys": 10,
    "values": 280,
    "metadata": 22
  }
}
```

Exact byte values will vary by device and row content; what matters is that all three `detailed` fields are present and non-negative.

---

### 3.4 Filesystem (new in v2.6.0)

**Native backing:** one JSON file per key, written under a dedicated subdirectory of the app's sandboxed storage:

- iOS: `<NSDocumentsDirectory>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`
- Android: `<Context.getFilesDir()>/strata_storage/<sanitised-key>.json`

The full `StorageValue` wrapper is JSON-serialised and written as file content. `keys()` lists the directory. `size()` sums the file sizes.

```typescript
async function testFilesystem() {
  const fsAdapter = new FilesystemAdapter();

  // Confirm the adapter reports itself as available on-device
  const available = await fsAdapter.isAvailable();
  console.assert(available === true, 'FAIL filesystem: isAvailable() returned false — plugin not wired?');

  const storage = defineStorage({
    defaultStorages: ['filesystem'],
  });
  storage.registerAdapter(fsAdapter);
  await storage.refreshAdapters();

  // --- set / get ---
  const testValue = { report: 'q1-2026', lines: 42 };
  await storage.set('fs_doc', testValue, { storage: 'filesystem' });

  const got = await storage.get<typeof testValue>('fs_doc', { storage: 'filesystem' });
  console.assert(got?.report === 'q1-2026', 'FAIL filesystem: get after set — report field wrong');
  console.assert(got?.lines === 42, 'FAIL filesystem: get after set — lines field wrong');

  // --- keys ---
  await storage.set('fs_doc_b', 'extra', { storage: 'filesystem' });
  const keys = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'filesystem' });
  console.assert(keys.includes('fs_doc'), 'FAIL filesystem: keys missing fs_doc');
  console.assert(keys.includes('fs_doc_b'), 'FAIL filesystem: keys missing fs_doc_b');

  // --- remove ---
  await storage.remove('fs_doc_b', { storage: 'filesystem' });
  const afterRemove = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'filesystem' });
  console.assert(!afterRemove.includes('fs_doc_b'), 'FAIL filesystem: key present after remove');

  // --- size ---
  const sizeInfo = await fsAdapter.size();
  console.assert(typeof sizeInfo.total === 'number' && sizeInfo.total > 0, 'FAIL filesystem: size().total not positive');
  console.assert(sizeInfo.count >= 1, 'FAIL filesystem: size().count is 0 after writing');

  // --- clear ---
  await storage.clear({ storage: 'filesystem' });
  const afterClear = await storage.keys(undefined, { storage: 'filesystem' });
  console.assert(afterClear.length === 0, 'FAIL filesystem: keys not empty after clear');

  console.log('PASS filesystem');
}
```

**Physical file verification (optional but recommended):**

On iOS simulator you can confirm the file actually exists via the Xcode Device & Simulators window: **Window > Devices and Simulators**, select your simulator, click the settings icon next to the app, and choose **Download Container**. Unzip the `.xcappdata` and look for `AppData/Documents/strata_storage/fs_doc.json`.

On Android emulator, use Android Studio's **Device File Explorer** (bottom-right panel): navigate to `data/data/<your.app.id>/files/strata_storage/`. After a successful `set`, `fs_doc.json` should be visible there.

---

### 3.5 `isAvailable` per storage type

Call `isAvailable()` on each adapter before running the full test matrix to confirm the plugin bridge is connected. If any of these return `false` unexpectedly, see §5 Troubleshooting.

```typescript
async function testIsAvailable() {
  const prefs = new PreferencesAdapter();
  const secure = new SecureAdapter();
  const sqlite = new SqliteAdapter();
  const fs = new FilesystemAdapter();

  const results = {
    preferences: await prefs.isAvailable(),
    secure: await secure.isAvailable(),
    sqlite: await sqlite.isAvailable(),
    filesystem: await fs.isAvailable(),
  };

  console.log('isAvailable results:', results);

  // All four must be true on both platforms
  Object.entries(results).forEach(([name, val]) => {
    console.assert(val === true, `FAIL isAvailable: ${name} returned false`);
  });

  console.log('PASS isAvailable');
}
```

**Expected platform matrix:**

| Storage type | iOS simulator | iOS real device | Android emulator | Android real device |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `preferences` | `true` | `true` | `true` | `true` |
| `secure` | `true` | `true` | `true` | `true` |
| `sqlite` | `true` | `true` | `true` | `true` |
| `filesystem` | `true` | `true` | `true` | `true` |

`isAvailable()` returns `false` on the web (non-Capacitor) platform by design — `isCapacitor()` guards the check. Running these tests in a browser tab will always return `false`.

---

## 5. Troubleshooting

### Plugin not registered — every call returns `undefined`

The JavaScript layer receives `undefined` from all native calls when the `CAP_PLUGIN` macro in `StrataStoragePlugin.m` is missing a method or the file was not compiled into the native target. Check:

1. Open `ios/Plugin/StrataStoragePlugin.m` and confirm the method you are calling appears in the `CAP_PLUGIN(StrataStoragePlugin, "StrataStorage", ...)` block. The full list for v2.6.0 should be:
   ```
   isAvailable, get, set, remove, clear, keys, size, query,
   getUserDefaults, setUserDefaults, getKeychain, setKeychain
   ```
   Filesystem operations go through the generic `get/set/remove/clear/keys/size` methods with `storage: 'filesystem'` — they do not require separate CAP_PLUGIN entries.
2. Run `npx cap sync ios` again to force-copy the updated `.m` file into the Xcode project, then clean the build (**Product > Clean Build Folder**, ⇧⌘K) and rebuild.

### iOS: `pod install` fails or plugin not found

- Confirm `strata-storage` appears in `ios/App/Podfile` (CocoaPods-based projects) after `cap sync`. If it does not, check that `node_modules/strata-storage/StrataStorage.podspec` exists and is valid.
- Run `pod repo update` then `pod install` again if the repo cache is stale.
- For SPM: make sure the local file reference in the Xcode package list points to the correct `strata-storage` directory. After `yarn build` re-runs, the SPM cache may need to be reset via **File > Packages > Reset Package Caches**.

### Android: `isAvailable()` returns `false` for `secure`

`EncryptedSharedPreferences` requires API level 23 (Android 6.0). Confirm `android/app/build.gradle` has `minSdkVersion 23` or higher. If the test runs on an older emulator image, upgrade the AVD to API 23+.

`androidx.security:security-crypto 1.1.0` (stable) may require bumping `compileSdkVersion` to 34. If Gradle sync fails with a `minCompileSdk(34)` error, update:

```groovy
// android/app/build.gradle
android {
    compileSdkVersion 34
    defaultConfig {
        minSdkVersion 23
        targetSdkVersion 34
    }
}
```

### Android: Gradle sync error `Could not resolve androidx.security:security-crypto:1.1.0`

Ensure the `google()` repository is listed in `android/build.gradle` (project-level):

```groovy
allprojects {
    repositories {
        google()
        mavenCentral()
    }
}
```

Then run **File > Sync Project with Gradle Files**.

### SQLite multi-store: both stores return the same value

The native `get`/`set`/`clear`/`keys` handlers receive `database` and `table` from the JS options object. If both stores still collide after the v2.6.0 update, log the raw Capacitor call options in the native handler to confirm the parameters arrive. On Android this is `call.getString("database")` in the Java handler; on iOS it is `call.getString("database")` in the Swift handler. A `nil` return means the JS adapter is not passing the parameter.

### Filesystem: `isAvailable()` returns `false`

The `FilesystemAdapter.isAvailable()` calls `StrataStorage.isAvailable({ storage: 'filesystem' })` through the plugin. The native handler must handle the `'filesystem'` case explicitly and return `{ available: true }`. If the handler has no `filesystem` branch it will fall through to an error or return `false`. Confirm the native dispatch table covers all four storage types.

### Xcode: `StrataStoragePlugin` class not found at runtime

Clean derived data — in Xcode go to **Product > Clean Build Folder** (⇧⌘K), delete `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`, then rebuild. If the class is still not found, confirm `StrataStoragePlugin.swift` is included in the target's **Compile Sources** build phase.

---

*Last updated: 2026-05-27 — covers strata-storage v2.6.0 native changes.*

# Firebase Sync Guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/firebase
================================================================================

# Firebase Sync Guide

Sync Strata Storage across devices and users with **Firebase** — either **Cloud
Firestore** or the **Realtime Database**. Firebase is an **optional peer
dependency**: it is loaded dynamically only when you call `enableFirebaseSync`,
so it adds nothing to your bundle unless you use it. The core package keeps its
zero-runtime-dependency guarantee.

## Installation

```bash
# the package itself
yarn add strata-storage

# Firebase is an OPTIONAL peer dependency — install it only if you use this feature
yarn add firebase
```

Import the Firebase helpers from the dedicated entry point:

```typescript
import { enableFirebaseSync, isFirebaseAvailable } from 'strata-storage/firebase';
```

## Quick start (Firestore)

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { enableFirebaseSync } from 'strata-storage/firebase';

const storage = defineStorage();

await enableFirebaseSync(storage, {
  apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY',
  authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com',
  projectId: 'your-app',
  appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID',
  firestore: true,            // register the Firestore adapter
  collectionName: 'strata-storage', // optional (this is the default)
});

// Use it like any other store — writes go to Firestore, and onSnapshot pushes
// remote changes back into your subscribers.
await storage.set('profile', { name: 'Ada' }, { storage: 'firestore' });
const profile = await storage.get('profile', { storage: 'firestore' });
```

## Quick start (Realtime Database)

```typescript
await enableFirebaseSync(storage, {
  apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY',
  authDomain: 'your-app.firebaseapp.com',
  projectId: 'your-app',
  appId: 'YOUR_APP_ID',
  realtimeDatabase: true, // register the Realtime Database adapter
});

await storage.set('counter', 1, { storage: 'realtime' });
```

You can enable **both** at once (`firestore: true, realtimeDatabase: true`) — each
registers its own adapter (`firestore` / `realtime`).

## Configuration — `FirebaseSyncConfig`

```typescript
interface FirebaseSyncConfig {
  apiKey: string;            // required — Firebase web API key
  authDomain: string;        // required
  projectId: string;         // required
  appId: string;             // required
  storageBucket?: string;
  messagingSenderId?: string;
  realtimeDatabase?: boolean; // register the Realtime Database adapter
  firestore?: boolean;        // register the Firestore adapter
  collectionName?: string;    // Firestore collection only (default: 'strata-storage'); the RTDB root is always 'strata-storage'
  syncInterval?: number;
}
```

`enableFirebaseSync` initializes the Firebase app if one is not already
initialized, then registers the requested adapter(s) on your `Strata` instance
via `registerAdapter`. Target them explicitly with `{ storage: 'firestore' }` or
`{ storage: 'realtime' }`, or add them to your `defaultStorages` order.

## How the adapters behave

| | `firestore` | `realtime` |
|---|---|---|
| Persistence | ✅ remote | ✅ remote |
| Observable (`subscribe`) | ✅ via `onSnapshot` | ✅ via `onValue` |
| Queryable | ✅ | ❌ |
| Storage layout | one document per key in `collectionName` | `strata-storage/<key>` |
| `size()` | returns `{ total: 0, count: 0 }` (not computed) | rough estimate |

Remote changes arrive through your `subscribe(...)` callback with
`source: 'remote'`, so you can distinguish them from local writes.

## Checking availability

```typescript
import { isFirebaseAvailable } from 'strata-storage/firebase';

if (await isFirebaseAvailable()) {
  await enableFirebaseSync(storage, config);
}
```

`isFirebaseAvailable()` resolves `true` only when the optional `firebase`
dependency can be imported.

## Caveats & best practices

- **These adapters are not encrypted at rest by Strata** (`encrypted: false`).
  Data is stored in Firebase as-is. If you need confidentiality, combine this
  with the [Encryption feature](../features/encryption.md) (encrypt values before
  they leave the device) and/or rely on Firebase Security Rules for access
  control.
- **Secure your Firebase project** with Auth + Security Rules — Strata does not
  manage authentication or authorization.
- `firestore.size()` is a stub (`{ total: 0, count: 0 }`); don't rely on it for
  quota math.
- Pricing/quotas are governed by Firebase, not Strata — design your read/write
  patterns accordingly.

## See also

- [Firebase examples](../../examples/firebase.md)
- [Sync feature](../features/sync.md)
- [Encryption guide](../features/encryption.md)

# iOS platform guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/ios
================================================================================

# iOS Platform Guide

Strata Storage's Capacitor plugin provides `preferences` (UserDefaults), `secure` (Keychain), `sqlite` and `filesystem` adapters on iOS.

## Installation

```bash
yarn add strata-storage
yarn cap sync ios
```

## Native Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory'],
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('theme', 'dark', { storage: 'preferences' });
await storage.set('draft:1', { title: 'First draft' }, { storage: 'sqlite' });
await storage.set('session_token', token, {
  storage: 'secure',
  ttl: 3_600_000,
});
```

The helper registers native adapters only inside a Capacitor app. Use the prepared `storage` instance throughout the application.

## Storage Choices

| Adapter | Use for | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| `preferences` | Small app settings | Not encrypted; no iCloud sync option in `StrataConfig` |
| `secure` | Sensitive key-value data | No biometric prompt or Keychain accessibility option in `StorageOptions` |
| `sqlite` | Larger structured key-value sets | Top-level `Strata` has no atomic `transaction()` API |
| `filesystem` | File-backed JSON values | Directory is fixed by the native adapter |

The Capacitor plugin definitions include lower-level Keychain and UserDefaults methods, but the `Strata` adapter options do not expose App Groups, a biometric requirement, iCloud sync, or a per-call directory. Use a separately verified native integration if your app needs one of those behaviors.

## Verification

Run the [native device matrix](./device-verification.md) on a simulator or device. Check values after force-quitting and relaunching the app, then confirm the native storage path used by each adapter. A browser test cannot prove Keychain, UserDefaults, SQLite or filesystem persistence.

## See Also

- [Capacitor guide](./capacitor.md)
- [SQLite adapter](../../api/adapters/capacitor/sqlite.md)
- [Secure adapter](../../api/adapters/capacitor/secure.md)

# Web platform guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/guides/platforms/web
================================================================================

# Web platform guide

Strata Storage's browser adapters give one key/value API over several browser storage facilities. The adapter you choose still determines persistence, quota and availability.

## Start with a browser-ready instance

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');
```

`defineStorage()` registers memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies and the Cache adapter. It initializes lazily. With no explicit `storage` option, Strata tries your `defaultStorages` in order and uses the first available registered adapter; it does not measure and choose the fastest backend.

To select a backend deliberately:

```typescript
await storage.set('setting', 'dark', { storage: 'localStorage' });
await storage.set('temporary', 'editing', { storage: 'memory' });
await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, {
  storage: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage'],
});
```

Web storage availability and quota depend on the browser, storage settings, browsing mode and device. Test each target browser and a reload round-trip. See the [adapter map](../../api/adapters/README.md) for what each adapter stores.

## Cross-tab changes

```typescript
const sharedStorage = defineStorage({ sync: { enabled: true } });
const unsubscribe = sharedStorage.subscribe(change => {
  if (change.source === 'remote') {
    // Refresh the affected view from storage.
  }
});

// Call unsubscribe() when this view is removed.
```

Cross-tab notifications do not make a write atomic across tabs. Use a server or a coordinated protocol for operations that must not be duplicated.

## Service workers

The Strata Cache adapter requires `window` and is for JSON-serializable key/value data in browser pages. It is not the browser's request/response cache interface inside a service worker. Use the browser Cache API for an app shell or HTTP responses in that scope:

```javascript
// In a service worker
self.addEventListener('install', event => {
  event.waitUntil((async () => {
    const cache = await caches.open('app-shell-v1');
    await cache.add('/index.html');
  })());
});
```

Choose a cache version and update policy for your app. The sample only shows installation and does not provide an offline fallback or an update flow.

## Quota and persistent storage

```typescript
if (navigator.storage?.estimate) {
  const estimate = await navigator.storage.estimate();
  // Inspect estimate.usage and estimate.quota for this browser.
}
```

`navigator.storage.persist()` is a browser permission request, not a guarantee that IndexedDB or Cache data survives every user action. Handle write failures and keep a recovery path for data that matters.

For an application outbox, see the [offline support example](../../examples/offline-support.md). The server must deduplicate replayed operations.

# Installation
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/installation
================================================================================

# Installation

Strata Storage 3.1.4 requires Node 24.13 or later in the toolchain and ships as ESM. The core package has no runtime dependencies. Framework, Firebase and Capacitor integrations are optional sub-path imports with their own peer requirements.

## Add the package

```bash
yarn add strata-storage
```

For another package manager, use its normal package-add command. The core browser entry point is `strata-storage`.

## Verify a browser write

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
await storage.set('installation-check', 'ready', { storage: 'memory' });
const result = await storage.get<string>('installation-check', {
  storage: 'memory',
});
console.log(result); // ready
```

`defineStorage()` registers the standard web adapters and initializes lazily. The memory check works in a browser page without asking for persistent storage. Then run the [Quick Start](./quick-start.md) with the adapter your app will use.

## Add a framework binding only when needed

The package exports `strata-storage/react`, `strata-storage/vue` and `strata-storage/angular`. Install the corresponding framework peer in your app and follow its [integration example](./examples/README.md). A basic `defineStorage()` call needs no framework Provider or plugin.

## Add Capacitor adapters only in a Capacitor app

Install the optional `@capacitor/core` peer through your app's package manager and sync the native project after installing the package. Register the adapters before selecting a native backend:

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage();
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);
await storage.set('device-setting', 'ready', { storage: 'preferences' });
const result = await storage.get<string>('device-setting', {
  storage: 'preferences',
});
```

This snippet requires a running Capacitor iOS or Android app. The registration helper returns without adding native adapters in a browser tab. Run the [device verification sequence](./guides/platforms/device-verification.md), including a read after app restart. The Secure adapter uses platform storage but does not expose a biometric prompt option; do not add Face ID usage text solely for this package.

## Optional Firebase integration

Install the `firebase` peer only if your app uses the [Firebase integration](./guides/platforms/firebase.md). Its setup and authentication remain your app's responsibility. The core package does not provide a hosted account or automatic cross-device synchronization.

## Encryption passwords

Do not put an encryption password in a browser `.env` file or compiled config: build tools can embed it in public JavaScript. An encrypted write needs an instance with encryption enabled **and** a password supplied by a user or other appropriate runtime flow. Follow the [encryption guide](./guides/features/encryption.md) for the exact options and recovery implications. A server secret belongs only on the server.

## Troubleshooting

- “No available storage adapters” usually means a manually constructed `new Strata()` instance has no registered adapters. Use `defineStorage()` for the standard browser set, or register the adapter explicitly.
- A native adapter cannot be selected from an ordinary browser page. Check Capacitor registration and the device runtime.
- If an encrypted write throws for a missing password, supply a password through the application flow; do not disable the failure or bundle a fixed one.

See [troubleshooting](./reference/troubleshooting.md) for further error paths.


================================================================================
# Introduction
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/
================================================================================

# Introduction

Strata Storage gives browser and Capacitor apps one `set()` and `get()` shape across several storage adapters. The adapter still matters: browser, iOS and Android values live in different places, and a browser read cannot prove a native read.

## First browser round-trip

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage();
await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' }, { storage: 'indexedDB' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft', {
  storage: 'indexedDB',
});
```

`defineStorage()` registers the standard browser adapters and initializes on first use. Memory, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies and a JSON-value Cache adapter are included. The URL adapter is registered separately for shareable UI state.

## What changes by platform

| Runtime | Available path | Verification boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Browser page | Standard web adapters through `defineStorage()` | Test the selected browser, quota and reload behaviour |
| Capacitor iOS/Android | Register Preferences, Secure, SQLite or Filesystem adapters | Run write → read → restart → read on a device |
| Node or server process | Memory and explicitly supported adapters | Do not assume a browser or native backend exists |

The native Secure adapter uses iOS Keychain or Android EncryptedSharedPreferences. Strata does not expose a biometric requirement or guarantee hardware-backed keys through its public options. Native adapter read paths still require [device verification](./guides/platforms/device-verification.md).

## Optional features

- Encryption and compression need an instance configured for those transforms. An encrypted write also needs an encryption password. Follow the [encryption](./guides/features/encryption.md) and [compression](./guides/features/compression.md) guides before enabling them.
- TTL can expire stored values. Query conditions match fields of the decoded value; wrapper metadata is not queryable. See [TTL](./guides/features/ttl.md) and the [query reference](./api/features/query.md).
- Cross-tab notifications can help refresh browser views. They do not make multi-tab writes atomic. Optional Firebase integration requires its own project and setup; it is not automatic cross-device sync.

## Next steps

1. [Install the package](./installation.md).
2. [Run the Quick Start](./quick-start.md).
3. [Choose an adapter](./api/adapters/README.md).
4. [Read the API reference](./api/core/strata.md).


================================================================================
# Strata Storage migration guide
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/migration
================================================================================

# Strata Storage Migration Guide

The main package exports the `Strata` class, but `new Strata()` starts with **no registered adapters**. Use `defineStorage()` for the standard web set, or register adapters explicitly before calling storage methods. Native adapters live in the `strata-storage/capacitor` entry point.

## Web Setup

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');
```

The factory registers the web adapters and initializes lazily on the first operation. Calling `initialize()` yourself is optional. A manual `new Strata()` setup must call `registerWebAdapters(storage)` or `storage.registerAdapter(...)` before use.

## Capacitor Setup

```typescript
import { Capacitor } from '@capacitor/core';
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';
import { registerCapacitorAdapters } from 'strata-storage/capacitor';

const storage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: Capacitor.isNativePlatform()
    ? ['sqlite', 'preferences', 'memory']
    : ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});
await registerCapacitorAdapters(storage);

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First draft' });
```

`registerCapacitorAdapters()` registers Preferences, SQLite, Secure and Filesystem on a native Capacitor platform, then refreshes the instance. It does nothing to native registration in a browser. Import it from the Capacitor subpath, not the package root.

## Existing Keys

The web `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` adapters now write with the `strata:` physical key prefix. The library can adopt its own older unprefixed storage envelopes on read. If an external script reads a physical key directly before Strata loads, configure `keyPrefix: false` and test that reader before upgrading; [configuration](./configuration.md#key-ownership) explains the ownership check.

## Verify the Migration

1. Build with the current package exports and inspect every custom `new Strata()` instance for registration.
2. Read a known pre-upgrade key, write a new value, reload and read it back.
3. On iOS and Android, sync the native project and run the [device verification guide](./guides/platforms/device-verification.md). Browser tests cannot prove native persistence.


================================================================================
# Quick Start
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/quick-start
================================================================================

# Quick Start

Your first `set()` needs an available adapter. The exported `storage` instance registers the standard web adapters and initialises on first use. You don't construct or initialise it.

<a id="install"></a>
## 📦 Install&nbsp;[#](#install)

```bash
yarn add strata-storage
```

The package is ESM-only and requires [Node 24.13 or later](https://github.com/aoneahsan/strata-storage/blob/main/package.json) in your toolchain. It has no runtime dependencies. React, Vue, Angular, Firebase and Capacitor integrations are optional sub-path imports with their own peer requirements.

<a id="write-and-read-a-value"></a>
## 🛠️ Write and read a value&nbsp;[#](#write-and-read-a-value)

```typescript
import { storage } from 'strata-storage';

await storage.set('draft', { title: 'First pass' });
const draft = await storage.get<{ title: string }>('draft');

console.log(draft?.title); // First pass

await storage.remove('draft');
console.log(await storage.has('draft')); // false
```

The default preference order is `localStorage`, `indexedDB`, `sessionStorage`, then `memory`. The instance also registers `cookies` and `cache`; `keys()`, `clear()` and `size()` without a storage option span all registered adapters. `subscribe()` listens to registered adapters that support change events. The URL adapter is exported but must be registered explicitly. See [storage selection](/configuration#storage-selection) before calling a broad `clear()`.

`get<T>()` returns `T | null` when you supply `T`; without it the result is `unknown | null`. The type parameter describes your data to TypeScript. It does not validate stored data at runtime.

<a id="configure-one-instance-for-your-app"></a>
## ⚙️ Configure one instance for your app&nbsp;[#](#configure-one-instance-for-your-app)

Use `defineStorage()` when you need a different adapter preference or feature set. It registers the standard web adapters and initialises lazily, just like `storage`.

```typescript
import { defineStorage } from 'strata-storage';

export const appStorage = defineStorage({
  defaultStorages: ['indexedDB', 'localStorage', 'memory'],
});

await appStorage.set('theme', 'dark');
const theme = await appStorage.get<string>('theme');
```

`defaultStorages` sets preference order; it does **not** limit which adapters are registered. To exclude an adapter, use `adapters: { <name>: false }` in the configuration. [Configuration](/configuration) explains adapter options and the `strata:` key prefix used by `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` since 3.0.

<a id="choose-a-framework-or-native-guide"></a>
## 📱 Choose a framework or native guide&nbsp;[#](#choose-a-framework-or-native-guide)

The core API works without a provider. For a framework, create an instance with `defineStorage()` and bind it:

- [React](/examples/frameworks/react): bind hooks with `createStrataHooks()`.
- [Vue](/examples/frameworks/vue): bind composables with `createStrataComposables()`.
- [Angular](/examples/frameworks/angular): provide an instance through `provideStrata()`.

On iOS and Android, register the Capacitor adapters, run `yarn cap sync`, and verify reads and writes on a device. A browser test does not exercise Keychain, EncryptedSharedPreferences, SQLite or the native filesystem. Follow the [device verification guide](/guides/platforms/device-verification).

<a id="explore-feature-guides-and-limits"></a>
## 🎛️ Explore feature guides and limits&nbsp;[#](#explore-feature-guides-and-limits)

- [Encryption](/guides/features/encryption) and [compression](/guides/features/compression) are opt-in and use the asynchronous API.
- [Expiry](/api/features/ttl) supports absolute or sliding TTL.
- [Queries](/guides/features/queries) filter stored values; Strata Storage remains client-side key-value storage, not a multi-user database.
- [Key-prefix migration](/configuration#key-prefix) moves qualifying 2.x `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` keys on read, not in a bulk sweep.
- If one browser app only needs `localStorage`, use it directly.

<a id="api-reference"></a>
## ➡️ API reference&nbsp;[#](#api-reference)

Open the [API reference](/api/core/strata) for method and option contracts, or try the [basic usage examples](/examples/basic-usage) for another round-trip.

# Changelog
URL: https://stratastorage-docs.aoneahsan.com/reference/changelog
